sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第088卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Scroll 88.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 88.

sentences.zh: 卷第八十八

translations.literal: Scroll the Eighty-eighth.
translations.idiomatic: Volume 88.

sentences.zh: 【晉紀十】起玄黓涒灘，盡昭陽作噩，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Jin Annals 10] Beginning in the year Xuanmo Tuoshan, ending in Zhaoyang Zuoe; in all, two years.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Annals, Part 10] This section runs from the second year of the sexagenary cycle (Xuanshi Tuoshan) through the thirty-eighth (Zhaoyang Zuoe)—two years in total.

sentences.zh: 孝懷皇帝下永嘉六年（

translations.literal: Below the Filial and Commiserating Emperor, the sixth year of Yongjia (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huai of Jin, the sixth year of the Yongjia era (

sentences.zh: 壬申，公元三一二年）

translations.literal: Renshen, corresponding to the year 312 CE).
translations.idiomatic: the year Renshen, 312 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，漢呼延後卒，謚曰武元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Han empress Lady Huyan died; her posthumous title was Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, Empress Huyan of Han died and was given the posthumous name Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 漢鎮北將軍靳沖、平北將軍卜珝寇并州；

translations.literal: The Han General Who Guards the North Jin Chong and the General Who Pacifies the North Bu Guang raided Bing Province;
translations.idiomatic: Han’s General Who Guards the North, Jin Chong, and General Who Pacifies the North, Bu Guang, invaded Bing Province;

sentences.zh: 辛未，圍晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day Xinwei, they besieged Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Xinwei they laid siege to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，漢主聰以司空王育、尚書令任顗女為左、右昭儀，中軍大將軍王彰、中書監范隆、左僕射馬景女皆為夫人，右僕射朱紀女為貴妃，皆金印紫綬。

translations.literal: On the day Jiaxu, the Han ruler Cong made the daughters of Minister of Works Wang Yu and Director of the Masters of Writing Ren Yi his Left and Right Zhaoyi; the daughters of General-in-Chief of the Center Army Wang Zhang, Director of the Secretariat Fan Long, and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Ma Jing were all made Ladies; the daughter of Right Vice Director Zhu Ji was made Noble Consort—all with gold seals and purple cords.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Jiaxu, Emperor Cong of Han appointed the daughters of Wang Yu, Minister of Works, and Ren Yi, Director of the Masters of Writing, as his Left and Right Zhaoyi; the daughters of Wang Zhang, General-in-Chief of the Center Army, Fan Long, Director of the Secretariat, and Ma Jing, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, were all made imperial ladies; Zhu Ji’s daughter, wife of the Right Vice Director, became Noble Consort—all bearing gold seals and purple sashes.

sentences.zh: 聰將納太保劉殷女，太弟乂固諫。

translations.literal: Cong was about to take in the daughters of Grand Guardian Liu Yin; the Grand Younger Brother Yi remonstrated firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Cong planned to marry the daughters of Grand Guardian Liu Yin, but his younger brother, the heir apparent Yi, protested vigorously.

sentences.zh: 聰以問太宰延年、太傅景，皆曰：「太保自雲劉康公之後，與隆下殊源，納之何害！」

translations.literal: Cong asked Grand Preceptor Yan Nian and Grand Tutor Jing; both said, "The Grand Guardian claims descent from Duke Kang of Liu; his line is a different source from Your Majesty—what harm in taking them in!"
translations.idiomatic: Cong consulted Grand Preceptor Yan Nian and Grand Tutor Jing. Both said, "The Grand Guardian says he descends from Duke Kang of the Liu house—a different lineage from yours. What harm could there be in marrying his daughters?"

sentences.zh: 聰悅，拜殷二女英、娥為左、右貴嬪，位在昭儀上；

translations.literal: Cong was pleased and enfeoffed Yin’s two daughters Ying and E as Left and Right Guibin, ranking above the Zhaoyi;
translations.idiomatic: Cong was pleased. He made Yin’s daughters Ying and E Left and Right Guibin, ranking above the Zhaoyi;

sentences.zh: 又納殷女孫四人皆為貴人，位次貴妃。

translations.literal: he also took in four granddaughters of Yin, all as Noble Ladies, ranking below the Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: and took four of Yin’s granddaughters as noble ladies, ranking just below the noble consort.

sentences.zh: 於是六劉之寵傾後宮，聰希復出外，事皆中黃門奏決。

translations.literal: Thereupon the favor of the six Liu women dominated the inner palace; Cong rarely went out again, and all affairs were reported and decided by the palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The six Liu women then dominated the harem. Cong seldom left the palace; eunuchs reported and decided everything.

sentences.zh: 故新野王歆牙門將胡亢聚眾於竟陵，自號楚公，寇掠荊土，以歆南蠻司馬新野杜曾為竟陵太守。

translations.literal: The former gate commander Hu Kang of Prince Xin of Xinye gathered a host at Jingling, styled himself Duke of Chu, and raided the Jing region; he made Du Zeng of Xinye, Southern Man Marshal of Xin, Jingling prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Kang, former gate commander to the deposed Prince Xin of Xinye, raised troops at Jingling, proclaimed himself Duke of Chu, and plundered Jing Province, appointing Du Zeng of Xinye—Southern Man marshal under Prince Xin—as prefect of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 曾勇冠三軍，能被甲游於水中。

translations.literal: Zeng’s courage surpassed all in the army; he could wear armor and swim in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng was the bravest man in the army and could fight in armor while swimming.

sentences.zh: 二月，壬子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day of the cycle (day Renzi), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the new moon (day Renzi), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 石勒築壘於葛陂，課農造舟，將攻建業。

translations.literal: Shi Le built fortifications at Gebei, set the farmers to building boats, and prepared to attack Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le fortified Gebei, pressed the peasants into building boats, and prepared to strike Jianye.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王睿大集江南之眾於壽春，以鎮東長史紀瞻為揚威將軍，都督諸軍以討之。

translations.literal: Prince Rui of Langye greatly gathered the hosts of Jiangnan at Shouchun, made the Eastern Garrison Chief Clerk Ji Zhan General Who Displays Might, and put him in overall command of the armies to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui of Langye massed Jiangnan’s forces at Shouchun, appointed his Eastern Garrison chief clerk Ji Zhan as General Who Displays Might, and gave him overall command to oppose Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 會大雨，三月不止，勒軍中饑疫，死者太半，聞晉軍將至，集將佐議之。

translations.literal: Just then heavy rain fell and did not stop for three months; in Le’s army famine and pestilence raged, and more than half died. Hearing that Jin forces were coming, he gathered his generals and aides to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains then fell for three months without cease. Famine and plague ravaged Le’s camp until more than half his men were dead. When word came that Jin armies were approaching, he called his officers to council.

sentences.zh: 右長史刁膺請先送款於睿，求掃平河朔以自贖，俟其軍退，徐更圖之，勒愀然長嘯。

translations.literal: The Right Chief Clerk Diao Ying asked first to send submission to Rui, seek to sweep the Hebei plain to redeem himself, and after the enemy army withdrew, slowly plot again; Le looked grim and gave a long whistle.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chief Clerk Diao Ying urged sending terms to Rui first, pacifying the north to atone, then striking again once the Jin army withdrew. Le’s face darkened and he gave a long whistle.

sentences.zh: 中堅將軍夔安請就高避水，勒曰：「將軍何怯邪！」

translations.literal: The Center-Stalwart General Kui An asked to move to high ground to avoid the water; Le said, "General, why so timid!"
translations.idiomatic: Center-Stalwart General Kui An proposed retreating to high ground to escape the floods. Le said, "General, why so faint-hearted?"

sentences.zh: 孔萇等三十餘將請各將兵，分道夜攻壽春，斬吳將頭，據其城，食其粟。

translations.literal: Kong Chang and more than thirty other generals asked each to lead troops by separate routes in a night attack on Shouchun, cut off the Wu generals’ heads, seize the city, and eat its grain.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang and thirty-odd other commanders volunteered to lead separate columns in a night assault on Shouchun, behead the Wu commanders, hold the city, and live off its grain stores.

sentences.zh: 要以今年破丹楊，定江南。

translations.literal: They vowed to break Danyang this year and settle Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: They pledged to smash Danyang this year and secure Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 勒笑曰：「是勇將之計也！」

translations.literal: Le laughed and said, "That is a brave general’s plan!"
translations.idiomatic: Le laughed. "A bold warrior’s scheme!"

sentences.zh: 各賜鎧馬一匹。

translations.literal: He gave each a suit of armor and a horse.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded each with a suit of armor and a horse.

sentences.zh: 顧謂張賓曰：「於君意何如？」

translations.literal: Turning to Zhang Bin he said, "What is your view?"
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Zhang Bin. "What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 賓曰：「將軍攻陷京師，囚執天子，殺害王公，妻略妃主。

translations.literal: Bin said, "The general stormed the capital, seized the Son of Heaven, killed kings and dukes, and took imperial consorts and princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "You stormed the capital, seized the emperor, slaughtered princes and nobles, and ravished imperial women.

sentences.zh: 擢將軍之發，不足以數將軍之罪，奈何復相臣奉乎！

translations.literal: Plucking out the general’s hair would not suffice to count the general’s crimes—how then submit and serve as minister again!
translations.idiomatic: Plucking every hair on your head would not exhaust your crimes—how could you now bow and serve them as a subject?

sentences.zh: 去年既殺王彌，不當來此；

translations.literal: Last year you already killed Wang Mi—you ought not to have come here;
translations.idiomatic: After killing Wang Mi last year you should never have come south;

sentences.zh: 今天降霖雨於數百里中，示將軍不應留此也。

translations.literal: now Heaven sends ceaseless rain across hundreds of li—this shows the general should not remain here.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven now sends endless rain across hundreds of miles—clearly you should not stay here.

sentences.zh: 鄴有三台之固，西接平陽，山河四塞，宜北徙據之，以經營河北，河北既定，天下無處將軍之右者矣。

translations.literal: Ye has the strength of the Three Platforms, links west to Pingyang, and is sealed on four sides by mountains and rivers—you should move north and hold it, manage Hebei; once Hebei is settled, nowhere in the realm will stand above the general.
translations.idiomatic: Ye is fortified by the Three Platforms, borders Pingyang to the west, and is boxed in by mountains and rivers. Move north and hold it, consolidate Hebei, and none in the realm will rival you.

sentences.zh: 晉之保壽春，畏將軍往攻之耳。

translations.literal: The Jin hold Shouchun only because they fear the general will attack.
translations.idiomatic: Jin holds Shouchun only because they fear you will strike.

sentences.zh: 彼聞吾去，喜於自全，何暇追襲吾後，為吾不利邪！

translations.literal: When they hear we are leaving they will rejoice at their own safety—how would they have leisure to pursue and strike from behind to our harm!
translations.idiomatic: When they hear we are leaving they will rejoice at being spared—why would they chase us or harm our retreat?

sentences.zh: 將軍宜使輜重從北道先發，將軍引大兵向壽春。

translations.literal: The general should send the baggage train north first; the general leads the main force toward Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Send your baggage train north first, then march the main army toward Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 輜重既遠，大兵徐還，何憂進退無地乎？」

translations.literal: Once the baggage is far off, the main force can withdraw slowly—why worry about having no room to advance or retreat?"
translations.idiomatic: Once the train is far ahead, withdraw the main body at leisure—what fear of being trapped?"

sentences.zh: 勒攘袂鼓髯曰：「張君計是也！」

translations.literal: Le rolled up his sleeves and stroked his beard and said, "Master Zhang’s plan is right!"
translations.idiomatic: Le rolled up his sleeves and tugged his beard. "Master Zhang is right!"

sentences.zh: 責刁膺曰：「君既相輔佐，當共成大功，奈何遽勸孤降！

translations.literal: He rebuked Diao Ying: "You were to assist me and together achieve great merit—why did you so quickly urge me to surrender!
translations.idiomatic: He turned on Diao Ying: "You were to help me win greatness—why urge surrender so soon?

sentences.zh: 此策應斬！

translations.literal: This counsel deserves execution!
translations.idiomatic: That advice deserves death!

sentences.zh: 然素知君怯，特相宥耳。」

translations.literal: Yet knowing your timidity of old, I specially spare you."
translations.idiomatic: But I have always known you for a coward, so I spare you."

sentences.zh: 於是黜膺為將軍，擢賓為右長史，號曰「右侯」。

translations.literal: Thereupon he demoted Ying to general and promoted Bin to Right Chief Clerk, styling him "Right Marquis."
translations.idiomatic: He demoted Ying to a field command and made Bin Right Chief Clerk, calling him "the Right Marquis."

sentences.zh: 勒引兵發葛陂，遣石虎帥騎二千向壽春，遇晉運船，虎將士爭取之，為紀瞻所敗。

translations.literal: Le led his army out from Gebei and sent Shi Hu with two thousand horse toward Shouchun; they met Jin transport boats, and Hu’s men scrambled to seize them but were defeated by Ji Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Le marched from Gebei and sent Shi Hu with two thousand cavalry toward Shouchun. They intercepted Jin supply boats; Hu’s men fought to seize them but Ji Zhan routed them.

sentences.zh: 瞻追奔百里，前及勒軍，勒結陳待之；

translations.literal: Zhan pursued a hundred li, came up to Le’s army, and Le formed battle lines to await him;
translations.idiomatic: Zhan pursued a hundred li and caught Le’s main force. Le drew up in battle order;

sentences.zh: 瞻不敢擊，退還壽春。

translations.literal: Zhan did not dare attack and withdrew to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan dared not attack and withdrew to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰封帝為會稽郡公，加儀同三司。

translations.literal: The Han ruler Cong enfeoffed the [Jin] emperor as Duke of Kuaiji and added the privilege of three departments’ ceremonial parity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cong of Han enfeoffed the captive Jin emperor as Duke of Kuaiji with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 聰從容謂帝曰：「卿昔為豫章王，朕與王武子造卿，武子稱朕於卿，卿言聞其名久矣，贈朕柘弓銀研，卿頗記否？」

translations.literal: Cong said at ease to the emperor, "When you were Prince of Yuzhang, I came to visit you with Wang Wuzi; Wuzi praised me to you, and you said you had long heard my name and gave me a catalpa bow and silver inkstone—do you quite remember?"
translations.idiomatic: Cong said casually to the emperor, "When you were Prince of Yuzhang, I visited you with Wang Wuzi. He praised me to you; you said you had long known my name and gave me a catalpa bow and a silver inkstone. Do you remember?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「臣安敢忘之？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "How would your servant dare forget?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "How could I forget?

sentences.zh: 但恨爾日不早識龍顏！」

translations.literal: I only regret that on that day I did not earlier recognize the dragon countenance!"
translations.idiomatic: I only regret that I did not recognize your imperial presence sooner that day!"

sentences.zh: 聰曰：「卿家骨肉何相殘如此？」

translations.literal: Cong said, "Why did your family’s flesh and blood slaughter one another so?"
translations.idiomatic: Cong said, "Why did your own kin tear one another apart like that?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「大漢將應天受命，故為陛下自相驅除，此殆天意，非人事也！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Great Han is about to receive the Mandate in response to Heaven; therefore for Your Majesty they drove one another out—this is likely Heaven’s intent, not human affair!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Great Han is destined to receive Heaven’s mandate, so we eliminated one another on your behalf. That was Heaven’s will, not mere human malice!

sentences.zh: 且臣家若能奉武皇帝之業，九族敦睦，陛下何由得之！」

translations.literal: Moreover, if my house could have upheld Emperor Wu’s enterprise and the nine clans lived in harmony, how would Your Majesty have obtained it!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, if our house had upheld Emperor Wu’s legacy and the clan had stayed united, how would you ever have taken the throne?"

sentences.zh: 聰喜，以小劉貴人妻帝，曰：「此名公子孫也，卿善遇之。」

translations.literal: Cong was pleased and gave the emperor the Younger Liu Noble Lady as wife, saying, "These are offspring of a famous house—treat her well."
translations.idiomatic: Cong was pleased. He gave the emperor a Liu lady of lesser rank as consort and said, "She is of a great house—treat her kindly."

sentences.zh: 代公猗盧遣兵救晉陽，三月，乙未，漢兵敗走。

translations.literal: The Duke of Dai Yilu sent troops to relieve Jinyang; in the third month, on the day Yiwei, the Han army was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Yilu of Dai sent troops to relieve Jinyang. In the third month, on the day Yiwei, the Han forces were routed.

sentences.zh: 卜珝之卒先奔，靳沖擅收珝，斬之；

translations.literal: Bu Guang’s troops fled first; Jin Chong on his own authority seized Guang and beheaded him;
translations.idiomatic: Bu Guang’s men broke first. Jin Chong seized him on his own authority and executed him;

sentences.zh: 聰大怒，遣使持節斬沖。

translations.literal: Cong was greatly angered and sent an envoy with credentials to execute Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was furious and sent an envoy with imperial credentials to execute Chong.

sentences.zh: 聰納其舅子輔漢將軍張實二女徽光、麗光為貴人，太后張氏之意也。

translations.literal: Cong took in the two daughters of his maternal nephew, the General Who Assists Han Zhang Shi—Huiguang and Liguang—as Noble Ladies, at Empress Dowager Zhang’s wish.
translations.idiomatic: At Empress Dowager Zhang’s urging, Cong took his nephew Zhang Shi’s daughters Huiguang and Liguang as noble ladies.

sentences.zh: 涼州主簿馬魴說張軌：「宜命將出師，翼戴帝室。」

translations.literal: The Liangzhou Registrar Ma Fang urged Zhang Gui: "You should order generals to take the field and support the imperial house."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Fang, registrar of Liang Province, urged Zhang Gui: "You should send generals to campaign in support of the imperial house."

sentences.zh: 軌從之，馳檄關中，共尊輔秦王，且言：「今遣前鋒督護宋配帥步騎二萬，逕趨長安；

translations.literal: Gui agreed, sent urgent proclamations through Guanzhong to honor jointly the Prince of Qin who assists the throne, and stated, "Now I send the vanguard Director Song Pei leading twenty thousand foot and horse straight for Chang’an;
translations.idiomatic: Gui agreed and issued urgent proclamations through Guanzhong to rally support for the Prince of Qin, saying, "I now send Vanguard Director Song Pei with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry straight for Chang’an;

sentences.zh: 西中郎將實帥中軍三萬，武威太守張琠帥胡騎二萬，絡繹繼發。」

translations.literal: the Western Central Commander of the Gentlemen Shi leads thirty thousand of the center army; the Administrator of Wuwei Zhang Yan leads twenty thousand barbarian horse—they will follow in continuous relays."
translations.idiomatic: Western Central Commander Shi will follow with thirty thousand of the center army, and Wuwei Administrator Zhang Yan with twenty thousand barbarian cavalry—all marching in succession."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙寅，征南將軍山簡卒。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day Bingyin, the General Who Conquers the South Shan Jian died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Bingyin, General Who Conquers the South Shan Jian died.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰封其子敷為渤海王，驥為濟南王，鸞為燕王，鴻為楚王，勱為齊王，權為秦王，操為魏王，持為趙王。

translations.literal: The Han ruler Cong enfeoffed his sons: Fu as Prince of Bohai, Ji as Prince of Jinan, Luan as Prince of Yan, Hong as Prince of Chu, Li as Prince of Qi, Quan as Prince of Qin, Cao as Prince of Wei, and Chi as Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cong enfeoffed his sons: Fu as Prince of Bohai, Ji as Prince of Jinan, Luan as Prince of Yan, Hong as Prince of Chu, Li as Prince of Qi, Quan as Prince of Qin, Cao as Prince of Wei, and Chi as Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 聰以魚蟹不供，斬左都水使者襄陵王攄；

translations.literal: Cong because fish and crab were not supplied beheaded the Left Director of Waterworks, Prince of Xiangling Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Cong executed Prince Shu of Xiangling, Left Director of Waterworks, because fish and crab were not supplied;

sentences.zh: 作溫明、徽光二殿未成，斬將作大匠望都公靳陵。

translations.literal: because the Warm Bright and Huiguang palaces were unfinished he beheaded the Master Builder of Works, Duke of Wangdu Jin Ling.
translations.idiomatic: and beheaded Duke Jin Ling of Wangdu, Master Builder, because the Warm Bright and Huiguang palaces were still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 觀漁於汾水，昏夜不歸。

translations.literal: He watched fishing on the Fen River and did not return until deep night.
translations.idiomatic: He went fishing on the Fen River and did not return until late at night.

sentences.zh: 中軍大將軍王彰諫曰：「比觀陛下所為，臣實痛心疾首。

translations.literal: General-in-Chief of the Center Army Wang Zhang remonstrated: "Observing lately what Your Majesty has done, your servant is truly heart-stricken.
translations.idiomatic: General-in-Chief Wang Zhang remonstrated: "Watching Your Majesty’s recent conduct fills me with anguish.

sentences.zh: 今愚民歸漢之志未專，思晉之心猶甚；

translations.literal: Now the common people’s resolve to submit to Han is not yet single-minded, and their longing for Jin is still strong;
translations.idiomatic: The common people are not yet wholeheartedly loyal to Han; many still yearn for Jin;

sentences.zh: 劉琨咫尺，刺客縱橫。

translations.literal: Liu Kun is within a stone’s throw, and assassins roam freely.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun is close at hand, and assassins are everywhere.

sentences.zh: 帝王輕出，一夫敵耳。

translations.literal: When an emperor or king goes out lightly, a single man can be his match.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler ventures out lightly, any lone man can strike him down.

sentences.zh: 願陛下改往修來，則億兆幸甚！」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will reform the past and cultivate the future—then the myriad people will be greatly blessed!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty mends your ways, the realm will be blessed indeed!"

sentences.zh: 聰大怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: Cong was greatly angered and ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Cong flew into a rage and ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 王夫人叩頭乞哀，乃囚之。

translations.literal: Lady Wang kowtowed and begged for mercy, and he was imprisoned instead.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang kowtowed and pleaded for his life, so Cong imprisoned him instead.

sentences.zh: 太后張氏以聰刑罰過差，三日不食；

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhang, because Cong’s punishments were excessive, went three days without eating;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhang fasted for three days to protest Cong’s excessive punishments;

sentences.zh: 太弟乂、單于粲輿櫬切諫。

translations.literal: the Grand Younger Brother Yi and the Chanyu Can came with coffins on their backs in earnest remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: and the heir apparent Yi and Chanyu Can carried coffins on their backs to plead with him.

sentences.zh: 聰怒曰：「吾豈桀、紂，而汝輩生來哭人！」

translations.literal: Cong said angrily, "Am I Jie or Zhou, that you lot were born to wail at people!"
translations.idiomatic: Cong snapped, "Am I Jie or Zhou of old, that you were born only to weep at me?"

sentences.zh: 太宰延年、太保殷等公卿、列侯百餘人，皆免冠涕泣曰：「陛下功高德厚，曠世少比，往也唐、虞，今則陛下。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Yan Nian, Grand Guardian Yin, and more than a hundred ministers and marquises all removed their caps and wept, saying, "Your Majesty’s merit is high and virtue profound, rarely matched in the age; in the past it was Tang and Yu—in the present it is Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Yan Nian, Grand Guardian Yin, and more than a hundred ministers and marquises bared their heads and wept: "Your Majesty’s merit and virtue are unmatched—what Tang and Yu were of old, you are today.

sentences.zh: 而頃來以小小不供，亟斬王公；

translations.literal: Yet lately for slight failures in supply you have repeatedly beheaded kings and dukes;
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately you have executed princes and nobles over trifling shortages;

sentences.zh: 直言忤旨，遽囚大將。

translations.literal: frank words that offended the intent, and at once imprisoned a great general.
translations.idiomatic: and imprisoned a great general for speaking plainly against your will.

sentences.zh: 此臣等竊所未解，故相與憂之，忘寢與食。」

translations.literal: This we privately cannot understand; therefore we share this worry and forget sleep and food."
translations.idiomatic: We cannot understand this, and our worry keeps us from sleep or food."

sentences.zh: 聰慨然曰：「朕昨大醉，非其本心，微公等言之，朕不聞過。」

translations.literal: Cong said with feeling, "Yesterday I was very drunk—it was not my true heart; had you not spoken, I would not have heard my fault."
translations.idiomatic: Cong sighed, "I was drunk last night—that was not my true intent. Without your words I would never have known my fault."

sentences.zh: 各賜帛百匹，使侍中持節赦彰曰：「先帝賴君如左右手，君著勳再世，朕敢忘之！

translations.literal: He gave each a hundred bolts of silk and had a Palace Attendant with credentials pardon Zhang, saying, "The late emperor relied on you as on left and right hand; you achieved merit for two reigns—how would I dare forget!
translations.idiomatic: He gave each a hundred bolts of silk and sent a Palace Attendant with credentials to pardon Zhang: "The late emperor relied on you as on his own hands; you have served two reigns with distinction—how could I forget?

sentences.zh: 此段之過，希君蕩然。

translations.literal: This stretch of fault—I hope you will dismiss it utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Please put this lapse behind us.

sentences.zh: 君能盡懷憂國，朕所望也。

translations.literal: That you can fully cherish concern for the state is what I hope for.
translations.idiomatic: I count on you to keep the realm’s welfare at heart.

sentences.zh: 今進君驃騎將軍、定襄郡公，後有不逮，幸數匡之！」

translations.literal: Now I advance you to General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Dingxiang; hereafter if I fall short, may you often correct me!"
translations.idiomatic: I now promote you to General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Dingxiang. When I err again, correct me often!"

sentences.zh: 王彌既死，漢安北將軍趙固、平北將軍王桑恐為石勒所並，欲引兵歸平陽。

translations.literal: After Wang Mi had died, the Han General Who Pacifies the North Zhao Gu and General Who Pacifies the North Wang Sang, fearing annexation by Shi Le, wished to lead their troops back to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Mi’s death, Han generals Zhao Gu and Wang Sang, fearing absorption by Shi Le, planned to march back to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 軍中乏糧，士卒相食，乃自□交磽津西渡，攻掠河北郡縣。

translations.literal: The army lacked grain and the soldiers ate one another; they then crossed west from Jiaoqiang Ford and raided the commanderies and counties of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies ran out and the men resorted to cannibalism. They crossed west from Jiaoqiang Ford and plundered Hebei’s prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 劉琨以其兄子演為魏郡太守，鎮鄴，固、桑恐演邀之，遣長史臨深為質於琨。

translations.literal: Liu Kun made his elder brother’s son Yan prefect of Wei Commandery, stationed at Ye; Gu and Sang feared Yan would intercept them and sent Chief Clerk Lin Shen as hostage to Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun posted his nephew Yan as prefect of Wei at Ye. Gu and Sang feared Yan would block their path and sent Chief Clerk Lin Shen as hostage.

sentences.zh: 琨以固為雍州刺史，桑為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Kun made Gu Inspector of Yong Province and Sang Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Kun appointed Gu Inspector of Yong and Sang Inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 賈疋等圍長安數月，漢中山王曜連戰皆敗，驅掠士女八萬餘口，奔於平陽。

translations.literal: Jia Pi and others besieged Chang’an for months; the Han Prince of Zhongshan Liu Yao was defeated in successive battles, drove off and seized more than eighty thousand men and women, and fled to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Pi and others besieged Chang’an for months. Han Prince Liu Yao lost battle after battle, seized more than eighty thousand civilians, and fled to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 秦王業自雍入於長安。

translations.literal: Prince Ye of Qin entered Chang’an from Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ye of Qin entered Chang’an from Yong.

sentences.zh: 五月，漢主聰貶曜為龍驤大將軍，行大司馬。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Han ruler Cong demoted Yao to General of Dragon Cavalry, acting Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Emperor Cong demoted Yao to General of Dragon Cavalry and acting Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 聰使河內王粲攻傅祗於三渚，右將軍劉參攻郭默於懷；

translations.literal: Cong sent Prince Can of Henei to attack Fu Zhi at Sanzhu and Right General Liu Can to attack Guo Mo at Huai;
translations.idiomatic: Cong sent Prince Can of Henei against Fu Zhi at Sanzhu and Right General Liu Can against Guo Mo at Huai;

sentences.zh: 會祗病薨，城陷，粲遷祗子孫並其士民二萬餘戶於平陽。

translations.literal: just then Zhi died of illness, the city fell, and Can moved Zhi’s descendants and more than twenty thousand households of his people to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi died of illness before the assault ended. The city fell, and Can relocated Zhi’s family and more than twenty thousand households to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 六月，漢主聰欲立貴嬪劉英為皇后。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Han ruler Cong wished to install Guibin Liu Ying as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Emperor Cong wished to make Guibin Liu Ying empress.

sentences.zh: 張太后欲立貴人張徽光，聰不得已，許之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhang wished to install Noble Lady Zhang Huiguang; Cong had no choice and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhang wanted Noble Lady Zhang Huiguang instead; Cong reluctantly agreed.

sentences.zh: 英尋卒。

translations.literal: Ying soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Ying died soon after.

sentences.zh: 漢大昌文獻公劉殷卒。

translations.literal: The Han Duke of Dachang, Literary and Manifest Liu Yin, died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin, Duke of Dachang with the posthumous title Literary and Manifest, died.

sentences.zh: 殷為相，不犯顏忤旨，然因事進規，補益甚多。

translations.literal: Yin as chancellor did not confront the countenance or oppose the intent, yet by occasions offered counsel and added much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor, Yin never confronted Cong directly, yet he offered timely counsel that did the state much good.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰每與群臣議政事，殷無所是非；

translations.literal: Whenever the Han ruler Cong discussed state affairs with his ministers, Yin offered no right or wrong;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cong discussed policy with his ministers, Yin never openly took sides;

sentences.zh: 群臣出，殷獨留，為聰敷暢條理，商榷事宜，聰未嘗不從之。

translations.literal: after the ministers left, Yin alone remained and for Cong laid out the reasoning clearly and weighed the matters; Cong never failed to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: After the others left, Yin stayed behind to explain matters clearly and advise on policy—and Cong always followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 殷常戒子孫曰：「事君當務幾諫。

translations.literal: Yin often admonished his descendants, saying, "In serving a ruler one should strive for subtle remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Yin often warned his descendants: "When you serve a ruler, remonstrate subtly.

sentences.zh: 凡人尚不可面斥其過，況萬乘乎！

translations.literal: Ordinary men still may not be rebuked to their face for their faults—how much less the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: You cannot even scold an ordinary man to his face—how much less an emperor!

sentences.zh: 夫幾諫之功，無異犯顏，但不彰君之過，所以為優耳。」

translations.literal: The merit of subtle remonstrance is no different from confronting the countenance, yet it does not display the ruler’s fault—therefore it is superior."
translations.idiomatic: Subtle remonstrance achieves what blunt confrontation does, without exposing the ruler’s faults—that is why it is better."

sentences.zh: 官至侍中、太保、錄尚書，賜劍履上殿、入朝不趨、乘輿入殿。

translations.literal: He reached the offices of Palace Attendant, Grand Guardian, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and was granted sword and shoes in the hall, no hurrying at court, and riding the imperial carriage into the hall.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Palace Attendant, Grand Guardian, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, with the privileges of wearing sword and shoes in the hall, not hurrying at court, and entering the hall by imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 然殷在公卿間，常恂恂有卑讓之色，故能處驕暴之國，保其富貴，不失令名，以壽考自終。

translations.literal: Yet among the ministers Yin was always deferential with a humble, yielding air; therefore he could dwell in a violent state, preserve wealth and honor, not lose a good name, and end his days in longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet among ministers he always showed humble deference, which let him survive a tyrant’s court, keep his wealth and reputation, and die at a ripe old age.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰以河間王易為車騎將軍，彭城王翼為衛將軍，並典兵宿衛。

translations.literal: The Han ruler Cong made Prince Yi of Hejian General of Chariots and Cavalry and Prince Ji of Pengcheng Defender General, both commanding troops on palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cong made Prince Yi of Hejian General of Chariots and Cavalry and Prince Ji of Pengcheng Defender General, both commanding the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 高平王悝為征南將軍，鎮離石；

translations.literal: Prince Min of Gaoping was made General Who Conquers the South and stationed at Lishi;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Min of Gaoping became General Who Conquers the South, stationed at Lishi;

sentences.zh: 濟南王驥為征西將軍，築西平城以居之；

translations.literal: Prince Ji of Jinan was made General Who Conquers the West and built Xiping city to dwell there;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji of Jinan became General Who Conquers the West and built Xiping to live in;

sentences.zh: 魏王操為征東將軍，鎮蒲子。

translations.literal: Prince Cao of Wei was made General Who Conquers the East and stationed at Puzi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cao of Wei became General Who Conquers the East, stationed at Puzi.

sentences.zh: 趙固、王桑自懷求迎於漢，漢主聰遣鎮遠將軍梁伏疵將兵迎之。

translations.literal: Zhao Gu and Wang Sang requested escort from Han at Huai; the Han ruler Cong sent the General Who Pacifies the Distance Liang Fuci with troops to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gu and Wang Sang asked Han for escort from Huai. Emperor Cong sent General Who Pacifies the Distance Liang Fuci to meet them.

sentences.zh: 未至，長史臨深、將軍牟穆帥眾一萬叛歸劉演。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Chief Clerk Lin Shen and General Mou Mu led ten thousand men in revolt and returned to Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Before Fuci arrived, Chief Clerk Lin Shen and General Mou Mu rebelled with ten thousand men and joined Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 固隨疵而西，桑引其眾東奔青州，固遣兵追殺之於曲梁，桑將張鳳帥其餘眾歸演。

translations.literal: Gu followed Fuci westward; Sang led his host east to Qing Province. Gu sent troops who killed Sang at Quliang; Sang’s general Zhang Feng led the remainder to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Gu marched west with Fuci; Sang fled east to Qing Province. Gu’s troops killed Sang at Quliang, and Sang’s general Zhang Feng took the survivors to Yan.

sentences.zh: 聰以固為荊州刺史、領河南太守，鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: Cong made Gu Inspector of Jing Province and concurrent Administrator of Henan, stationed at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cong appointed Gu Inspector of Jing and concurrent Administrator of Henan, stationed at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 石勒自葛陂北行，所過皆堅壁清野，虜掠無所獲，軍中饑甚，士卒相食。

translations.literal: Shi Le marched north from Gebei; everywhere he passed they strengthened walls and cleared the countryside, and he seized nothing—the army was extremely hungry and the soldiers ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le marched north from Gebei. Everywhere he passed the people had fortified and stripped the land, so he captured nothing. Famine drove his men to cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 至東燕，聞汲郡向冰聚眾數千壁枋頭，勒將濟河，恐冰邀之。

translations.literal: Reaching Dongyan he heard that Xiang Bing of Ji Commandery had gathered several thousand and fortified Fangtou; Le was about to cross the river and feared Bing would intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: At Dongyan he learned that Xiang Bing of Ji had gathered thousands at Fangtou. Le was about to cross the Yellow River and feared Bing would block him.

sentences.zh: 張賓曰：「聞冰船盡在瀆中未上，宜遣輕兵間道襲取，以濟大軍，大軍既濟，冰必可擒也。」

translations.literal: Zhang Bin said, "I hear Bing’s boats are all in the sluice and not yet brought up—you should send light troops by a hidden route to seize them and ferry the main army; once the main army has crossed, Bing can surely be captured."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin said, "Bing’s boats are still in the sluice. Send light troops by a hidden path to seize them and ferry the army across. Once we cross, Bing will be ours."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，勒使支雄、孔萇自文石津縛筏潛渡，取其船。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Le had Zhi Xiong and Kong Chang bind rafts at Wenshi Ford and cross secretly, taking the boats.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Le had Zhi Xiong and Kong Chang raft across secretly at Wenshi Ford and seize the boats.

sentences.zh: 勒引兵自棘津濟河，擊冰，大破之，盡得其資儲，軍勢復振，遂長驅至鄴。

translations.literal: Le led his army across at Jiji Ford, struck Bing, and routed him, taking all his stores; the army’s momentum revived, and he drove on to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Le crossed at Jiji Ford, routed Bing, and seized all his supplies. His army revived and marched on to Ye.

sentences.zh: 劉演保三台以自固，臨深、牟穆等復帥其眾降於勒。

translations.literal: Liu Yan held the Three Platforms to defend himself; Lin Shen, Mou Mu, and others again led their hosts in surrender to Le.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan held the Three Platforms. Lin Shen, Mou Mu, and others surrendered to Le again.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲攻三台，張賓曰：「演雖弱，眾猶數千，三台險固，攻之未易猝拔。

translations.literal: The generals wished to attack the Three Platforms; Zhang Bin said, "Though Yan is weak, his men still number thousands; the Three Platforms are steep and strong—not easy to take in a rush.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to assault the Three Platforms. Zhang Bin said, "Yan is weak but still has thousands; the Platforms are steep—not easily taken at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 捨而去之，彼將自潰。

translations.literal: Leave them and go on—he will collapse of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Leave him and move on—he will fall apart on his own.

sentences.zh: 方今王彭祖、劉越石，公之大敵也，宜先取之，演不足顧也。

translations.literal: Now Wang Pengzu and Liu Yueshi are your great foes and should be taken first; Yan is not worth troubling over.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pengzu and Liu Yueshi are your real enemies—deal with them first. Yan is not worth the trouble.

sentences.zh: 且天下饑亂，明公雖擁大兵，遊行羈旅，人無定志，非所以保萬全，制四方也。

translations.literal: Moreover, with famine and chaos throughout the realm, though you hold a great army you wander as a guest and men have no fixed will—this is not how to secure complete safety and control the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is starving and in chaos. Though you command a great army, you are still a wanderer and your men have no settled loyalty—that is no way to secure the realm.

sentences.zh: 不若擇便地而據之，廣聚糧儲，西稟平陽以圖幽、并，此霸王之業也。

translations.literal: Better choose a convenient place and hold it, gather grain in abundance, and turn west to Pingyang to plan for You and Bing—this is the work of a hegemon-king.
translations.idiomatic: Choose a strong base, stock grain, and link with Pingyang to take You and Bing—that is how hegemons are made.

sentences.zh: 邯鄲、襄國，形勝之地，請擇一而都之。」

translations.literal: Handan and Xiangguo are places of strategic advantage—please choose one and make it your capital."
translations.idiomatic: Handan and Xiangguo are both strong sites—make one your capital."

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「右侯之計是也。」

translations.literal: Le said, "The Right Marquis’s plan is right."
translations.idiomatic: Le said, "The Right Marquis is right."

sentences.zh: 遂進據襄國。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced and occupied Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and took Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 賓復言於勒曰：「今吾居此，彭祖、越石所深忌也，恐城塹未固，資儲未廣，二寇交至。

translations.literal: Bin again said to Le, "Now that we dwell here, Pengzu and Yueshi will deeply resent it; I fear before walls and stores are ready both foes will come together.
translations.idiomatic: Bin warned Le, "Pengzu and Yueshi will hate our settling here. Before our walls and granaries are ready, both may strike.

sentences.zh: 宜亟收野谷，且遣使至平陽，具陳鎮此之意。」

translations.literal: You should quickly gather wild grain and send envoys to Pingyang stating fully your intent to hold this place."
translations.idiomatic: Gather wild grain at once and send envoys to Pingyang explaining why we hold this place."

sentences.zh: 勒從之，分命諸將攻冀州，郡縣壁壘多降，運其谷以輸襄國；

translations.literal: Le agreed, ordered his generals to attack Ji Province—many walled places surrendered—and transported their grain to Xiangguo;
translations.idiomatic: Le agreed, sent generals against Ji—many strongholds surrendered—and shipped grain to Xiangguo;

sentences.zh: 且表於漢主聰，聰以勒為都督冀、幽、并、營四州諸軍事、冀州牧，進封上黨公。

translations.literal: he also memorialized the Han ruler Cong, who made Le Commander over military affairs in Ji, You, Bing, and Ying and Inspector of Ji, and advanced him to Duke of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: he memorialized Emperor Cong, who made him commander over Ji, You, Bing, and Ying, Inspector of Ji, and Duke of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 劉琨移檄州郡，期以十月會平陽，擊漢。

translations.literal: Liu Kun issued proclamations to the provinces and commanderies, fixing the tenth month for a rendezvous at Pingyang to attack Han.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun called the provinces to muster at Pingyang in the tenth month to attack Han.

sentences.zh: 琨素奢豪，喜聲色。

translations.literal: Kun had always been extravagant and fond of music and women.
translations.idiomatic: Kun had always been extravagant and fond of pleasure.

sentences.zh: 河南徐潤以音律得幸於琨，琨以為晉陽令。

translations.literal: Xu Run of Henan, who won Kun’s favor through music, was made magistrate of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Run of Henan, who pleased Kun with music, was made magistrate of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 潤驕恣，干預政事。

translations.literal: Run was arrogant and meddled in government.
translations.idiomatic: Run grew arrogant and meddled in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 護軍令狐盛數以為言，且勸琨殺之，琨不從。

translations.literal: Protector of the Army Linghu Sheng spoke of this repeatedly and urged Kun to kill him; Kun would not.
translations.idiomatic: Protector Linghu Sheng repeatedly urged Kun to kill Run; Kun refused.

sentences.zh: 潤譖盛於琨，琨收盛，殺之。

translations.literal: Run slandered Sheng to Kun; Kun arrested Sheng and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Run slandered Sheng; Kun arrested and executed him.

sentences.zh: 琨母曰：「汝不能駕御豪傑以恢遠略，而專除勝己，禍必及我。」

translations.literal: Kun’s mother said, "You cannot control heroes to recover a far-reaching plan, yet you specialize in removing those who surpass you—disaster will reach me."
translations.idiomatic: Kun’s mother said, "You cannot command great men for a grand strategy, yet you destroy those who outshine you—disaster will find us."

sentences.zh: 盛子泥奔漢，具言虛實。

translations.literal: Sheng’s son Ni fled to Han and reported the full situation.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng’s son Ni fled to Han and revealed Kun’s weakness.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰大喜，遣河內王粲、中山王曜將兵寇并州，以令狐泥為鄉導。

translations.literal: The Han ruler Cong was greatly pleased and sent Prince Can of Henei and Prince Yao of Zhongshan with troops to raid Bing, with Linghu Ni as guide.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cong was delighted and sent Prince Can of Henei and Prince Yao of Zhongshan against Bing, with Linghu Ni as guide.

sentences.zh: 琨聞之，東出，收兵於常山及中山，使其將郝詵、張喬將兵拒粲，且遣使求救於代公猗盧。

translations.literal: When Kun heard, he went east, gathered troops in Changshan and Zhongshan, sent his generals Hao Shen and Zhang Qiao to resist Can, and dispatched envoys to beg aid from Duke Yilu of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Kun marched east, gathered troops in Changshan and Zhongshan, sent Hao Shen and Zhang Qiao against Can, and begged Duke Yilu of Dai for aid.

sentences.zh: 詵喬俱敗死。

translations.literal: Shen and Qiao were both defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and Qiao were defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 粲、曜乘虛襲晉陽，太原太守高喬、并州別駕郝聿以晉陽降漢。

translations.literal: Can and Yao seized the opening and struck Jinyang; Administrator Gao Qiao and Bingzhou Aide Hao Yu surrendered Jinyang to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Can and Yao struck Jinyang. Administrator Gao Qiao and Aide Hao Yu surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚戌，琨還救晉陽，不及，帥左右數十騎奔常山。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day Gengxu, Kun returned to relieve Jinyang but was too late; he fled to Changshan with only a few dozen horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Gengxu in the eighth month Kun rushed back too late and fled to Changshan with a few dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，粲、曜入晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day Xinhai, Can and Yao entered Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On Xinhai, Can and Yao entered Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 壬子，令狐泥殺琨父母。

translations.literal: On the day Renzi, Linghu Ni killed Kun’s parents.
translations.idiomatic: On Renzi, Linghu Ni killed Kun’s parents.

sentences.zh: 粲、曜送尚書盧志、侍中許遐、太子右衛率崔瑋於平陽。

translations.literal: Can and Yao sent Minister of Writing Lu Zhi, Palace Attendant Xu Xia, and Right Leader of the Heir Apparent’s Guard Cui Wei to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Can and Yao sent Lu Zhi, Xu Xia, and Cui Wei to Pingyang as prisoners.

sentences.zh: 聰復以曜為車騎大將軍，以前將軍劉豐為并州刺史，鎮晉陽。

translations.literal: Cong again made Yao General of Chariots and Cavalry and the former Forward General Liu Feng Inspector of Bing, stationed at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cong restored Yao as General of Chariots and Cavalry and made Liu Feng Inspector of Bing at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，聰以盧志為太弟太師，崔瑋為太傅，許遐為太保，高喬、令狐泥皆為武衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Cong made Lu Zhi Grand Tutor to the Grand Younger Brother, Cui Wei Grand Tutor, Xu Xia Grand Guardian, and Gao Qiao and Linghu Ni both Generals of Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Cong made Lu Zhi Grand Tutor to the heir apparent, Cui Wei Grand Tutor, Xu Xia Grand Guardian, and Gao Qiao and Linghu Ni Generals of Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 己卯，漢衛尉梁芬奔長安。

translations.literal: On the day Jimao, Han Defender of the Realm Liang Fen fled to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: On Jimao, Han Defender Liang Fen fled to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，賈疋等奉秦王業為皇太子，建行台於長安，登壇告類，建宗廟、社稷，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day Xinsi, Jia Pi and others installed Prince Ye of Qin as crown prince, established an executive office at Chang’an, sacrificed to Heaven, founded ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On Xinsi, Jia Pi and others made Prince Ye of Qin crown prince, set up an executive at Chang’an, sacrificed to Heaven, founded temple and altars, and declared amnesty.

sentences.zh: 以閻鼎為太子詹事，總攝百揆；

translations.literal: Yan Ding was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent with overall charge of all affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ding became Grand Tutor to the heir apparent with overall authority;

sentences.zh: 加賈疋征西大將軍，以秦州刺史南陽王保為大司馬。

translations.literal: Jia Pi was advanced to General Who Conquers the West, and Prince Bao of Nanyang, Inspector of Qin, was made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Pi was promoted to General Who Conquers the West and Prince Bao of Nanyang became Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 命司空荀籓督攝遠近，光祿大夫荀組領司隸校尉、行豫州刺史，與籓共保開封。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xun Fan was ordered to oversee near and far; Palace Counselor Xun Zu was made Director of the Masters of Writing with acting authority as Inspector of Yu, and with Fan together guarded Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xun Fan was to oversee the realm; Xun Zu became Director of the Masters of Writing, acting Inspector of Yu, and with Fan held Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 秦州刺史裴苞據險以拒涼州兵，張實、宋配等擊破之，苞奔柔凶塢。

translations.literal: Inspector Pei Bao of Qin held difficult terrain against Liangzhou troops; Zhang Shi, Song Pei, and others defeated him, and Bao fled to Rouxiong Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Inspector Pei Bao blocked Liangzhou’s army; Zhang Shi and Song Pei defeated him and Bao fled to Rouxiong Stockade.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，漢主聰封其子恆為代王，逞為吳王，朗為穎川王，皋為零陵王，旭為丹楊王，京為蜀王，坦為九江王，晃為臨川王；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Han ruler Cong enfeoffed his sons: Heng as Prince of Dai, Cheng as Prince of Wu, Lang as Prince of Yingchuan, Gao as Prince of Lingling, Xu as Prince of Danyang, Jing as Prince of Shu, Tan as Prince of Jiujiang, Huang as Prince of Linchuan;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Cong enfeoffed his sons Heng, Cheng, Lang, Gao, Xu, Jing, Tan, and Huang as princes of Dai, Wu, Yingchuan, Lingling, Danyang, Shu, Jiujiang, and Linchuan;

sentences.zh: 以王育為太保，王彰為太尉，任顗為司徒，馬景為司空，朱紀為尚書令，范隆為左僕射，呼延晏為右僕射。

translations.literal: he made Wang Yu Grand Guardian, Wang Zhang Grand Commandant, Ren Yi Minister of Works, Ma Jing Minister of Ceremonies, Zhu Ji Director of the Masters of Writing, Fan Long Left Vice Director, and Huyan Yan Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed Wang Yu Grand Guardian, Wang Zhang Grand Commandant, Ren Yi Minister of Works, Ma Jing Minister of Ceremonies, Zhu Ji Director of the Masters of Writing, Fan Long Left Vice Director, and Huyan Yan Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 代公猗盧遣其子六修及兄子普根、將軍衛雄、范班、箕澹帥眾數萬為前鋒以攻晉陽，猗盧自帥眾二十萬繼之，劉琨收散卒數千為之鄉導。

translations.literal: Duke Yilu of Dai sent his son Liuxiu and his brother’s son Pugen and the generals Wei Xiong, Fan Ban, and Ji Dan with tens of thousands as vanguard against Jinyang; Yilu himself followed with two hundred thousand, and Liu Kun gathered several thousand scattered troops as guides.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Yilu sent his son Liuxiu, nephew Pugen, and generals Wei Xiong, Fan Ban, and Ji Dan with tens of thousands against Jinyang; Yilu followed with two hundred thousand, and Kun gathered scattered troops as guides.

sentences.zh: 六修與漢中山王曜戰於汾東，曜兵敗，墜馬，中匕創。

translations.literal: Liuxiu fought Prince Yao of Zhongshan east of the Fen; Yao’s army was defeated, he fell from his horse, and was wounded by a dagger.
translations.idiomatic: Liuxiu fought Prince Yao east of the Fen. Yao was routed, fell from his horse, and was stabbed.

sentences.zh: 討虜將軍傅虎以馬授曜，曜不受，曰：「卿光乘以自免，吾創已重，自分死此。」

translations.literal: General Who Punishes the Barbarians Fu Hu gave Yao his horse; Yao would not take it and said, "You ride away on a swift mount; my wound is grave—I resign myself to die here."
translations.idiomatic: General Fu Hu offered Yao his horse. Yao refused: "Save yourself on a swift horse; my wound is mortal—I stay to die."

sentences.zh: 虎泣曰：「虎蒙大王識拔至此，常思效命，今其時矣。

translations.literal: Hu wept and said, "Hu owes his place to the great king’s recognition and has long wished to give his life—now is the time.
translations.idiomatic: Hu wept: "You raised me to this rank; I have long wished to die for you—now is the time.

sentences.zh: 且漢室初基，天下可無虎，不可無大王也！」

translations.literal: The Han house is newly founded—the realm can do without Hu but not without the great king!"
translations.idiomatic: Han is newly founded—the realm can spare me but not you!"

sentences.zh: 乃扶曜上馬，驅令渡汾，自還戰死。

translations.literal: He helped Yao mount, drove him across the Fen, and returned to fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: He helped Yao mount, forced him across the Fen, and returned to die fighting.

sentences.zh: 曜入晉陽，夜，與大將軍粲、鎮北大將軍豐掠晉陽之民，逾蒙山而歸。

translations.literal: Yao entered Jinyang; that night with Grand General Can and General Who Guards the North Feng he plundered the people of Jinyang, crossed Meng Mountain, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yao entered Jinyang. That night he and Can and Feng plundered the city, crossed Meng Mountain, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十一月，猗盧追之，戰於藍谷，漢兵大敗，擒劉豐，斬邢延等三千餘級，伏屍數百里。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Yilu pursued; they fought at Langu Valley—the Han army was routed, Liu Feng was captured, and Xing Yan and more than three thousand others were beheaded; corpses lay for hundreds of li.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yilu pursued to Langu Valley. The Han army was shattered; Liu Feng was captured and more than three thousand, including Xing Yan, were beheaded—corpses stretched for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 猗盧因大獵壽陽山，陳閱皮肉，山為之赤。

translations.literal: Yilu then held a great hunt on Shouyang Mountain, displaying meat and hides—the mountain turned red.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu held a great hunt on Shouyang Mountain and displayed the meat and hides until the mountain turned red.

sentences.zh: 劉琨自營門步入拜謝，固請進軍。

translations.literal: Liu Kun entered from the camp gate, bowed in thanks, and firmly urged an advance.
translations.idiomatic: Kun entered the camp gate, bowed in thanks, and pressed for a further advance.

sentences.zh: 猗盧曰：「吾不早來，致卿父母見害，誠以相愧。

translations.literal: Yilu said, "Had I come earlier your parents would not have been killed—I am truly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu said, "Had I come sooner your parents would still live—I am ashamed.

sentences.zh: 今卿已復州境，吾遠來，士馬疲弊，且待後舉，劉聰未可滅也。」

translations.literal: Now you have recovered your province; I came from afar and my men and horses are weary—we must wait for another campaign; Liu Cong cannot yet be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: You have recovered your province; my men are exhausted. We must wait—Liu Cong is not yet to be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 遣琨馬、牛、羊各千餘匹，車百乘而還，留其將箕澹、段繁等戍晉陽。

translations.literal: He gave Kun more than a thousand each of horses, cattle, and sheep, a hundred carts, and returned, leaving his generals Ji Dan and Duan Fan to garrison Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Kun a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep each, a hundred carts, and withdrew, leaving Ji Dan and Duan Fan to garrison Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 琨徙居陽曲，招集亡散。

translations.literal: Kun moved to Yangqu and gathered the scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Kun moved to Yangqu and gathered refugees.

sentences.zh: 盧諶為劉粲參軍，亡歸琨，漢人殺其父志及弟謐、詵。

translations.literal: Lu Chen was an aide to Liu Can and fled back to Kun; Han men killed his father Zhi and brothers Mi and Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chen, aide to Liu Can, fled to Kun; Han men killed his father Zhi and brothers Mi and Shen.

sentences.zh: 贈傅虎幽州刺史。

translations.literal: Fu Hu was posthumously made Inspector of You.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hu was posthumously made Inspector of You.

sentences.zh: 十二月，漢主聰立皇后張氏，以其父實為左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Han ruler Cong installed Empress Zhang and made her father Shi Left Palace Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Cong installed Empress Zhang and made her father Shi Left Palace Counselor.

sentences.zh: 彭仲蕩之子天護帥群胡攻賈疋，天護陽不勝而走，疋追之，夜墜澗中，天護執而殺之。

translations.literal: Peng Tianhu, son of Peng Zhongdang, led tribal forces against Jia Pi; Tianhu pretended defeat and fled, Pi pursued, fell into a ravine at night, and Tianhu seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Tianhu, son of Peng Zhongdang, attacked Jia Pi. Tianhu feigned retreat; Pi pursued, fell into a ravine at night, and Tianhu killed him.

sentences.zh: 漢以天護為涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Han made Tianhu Inspector of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Han made Tianhu Inspector of Liang.

sentences.zh: 眾推始平太守麴允領雍州刺史。

translations.literal: The masses pushed Qu Yun, Administrator of Shiping, to act as Inspector of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The people made Qu Yun of Shiping acting Inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 閻鼎與京兆太守梁綜爭權，鼎遂殺綜。

translations.literal: Yan Ding struggled for power with Administrator Liang Zong of Jingzhao and killed Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ding fought Liang Zong, Administrator of Jingzhao, for power and killed him.

sentences.zh: 麴允與撫夷護軍索綝、馮翊太守梁肅合兵攻鼎，鼎出奔雍，為氐竇首所殺。

translations.literal: Qu Yun with Protector Suo Lin and Administrator Liang Su of Fufeng combined forces against Ding; Ding fled to Yong and was killed by the Di leader Dou Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun, Suo Lin, and Liang Su attacked Ding; Ding fled to Yong and was killed by the Di leader Dou Shou.

sentences.zh: 廣平游綸、張豺擁眾數萬，據苑鄉，受王浚假署；

translations.literal: You Lun and Zhang Chai of Guangping held tens of thousands at Yuanxiang under acting commission from Wang Jun;
translations.idiomatic: You Lun and Zhang Chai of Guangping held tens of thousands at Yuanxiang under Wang Jun’s commission;

sentences.zh: 石勒遣夔安、支雄等七將攻之，破其外壘。

translations.literal: Shi Le sent Kui An, Zhi Xiong, and seven other generals against them and broke their outer ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent Kui An, Zhi Xiong, and seven generals, who breached their outer walls.

sentences.zh: 浚遣督護王昌帥諸軍及遼西公段疾陸眷、疾陸眷弟匹磾、文鴦、從弟末柸部眾五萬攻勒於襄國。

translations.literal: Jun sent Supervisor Wang Chang with all his armies and Duke Jilu of Liaoxi, his brother Pidi, Wen Yang, and cousin Mozhe with fifty thousand to attack Le at Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent Supervisor Wang Chang with his armies and Duke Jilu of Liaoxi, Pidi, Wen Yang, and cousin Mozhe with fifty thousand against Le at Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 疾陸眷屯於渚陽，勒遣諸將出戰，皆為疾陸眷所敗。

translations.literal: Jilu encamped at Zhuyang; Le sent generals out to fight and all were defeated by Jilu.
translations.idiomatic: Jilu camped at Zhuyang. Le’s generals sallied and were all defeated.

sentences.zh: 疾陸眷大造攻具，將攻城，勒眾甚懼。

translations.literal: Jilu built great siege engines and was about to storm the city; Le’s host was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Jilu built siege engines to storm the city; Le’s men were terrified.

sentences.zh: 勒召將佐謀之曰：「今城塹未固，糧儲不多，彼眾我寡，外無救授，吾欲悉眾與之決戰，何如？」

translations.literal: Le summoned his officers and said, "Walls are not yet firm and stores are few; they are many and we few, with no outside aid—I wish to stake all on a decisive battle—what say you?"
translations.idiomatic: Le asked his officers: "Our walls are weak, our grain low, they outnumber us, and no help is coming—shall we stake everything on one battle?"

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「不如堅守以疲敵，待其退而擊之。」

translations.literal: The generals all said, "Better hold firm to wear them down and strike when they withdraw."
translations.idiomatic: All said, "Hold fast, wear them down, and strike when they retreat."

sentences.zh: 張賓、孔萇曰：「鮮卑之種，段氏最為勇悍，而末柸尤甚，其銳卒皆在末柸所。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin and Kong Chang said, "Among the Xianbei tribes the Duan are bravest, and Mozhe above all; his crack troops are all in Mozhe’s command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin and Kong Chang said, "Of the Xianbei the Duan are bravest, especially Mozhe—all his elite are with Mozhe.

sentences.zh: 今聞疾陸眷刻日攻北城，其大眾遠來，戰鬥連日，謂我孤弱，不敢出戰，意必懈惰；

translations.literal: Now we hear Jilu will attack the north wall on a set day; his main host came from afar and has fought day after day, thinking us weak and afraid to sally—they will surely grow slack;
translations.idiomatic: Jilu will attack the north wall soon. His main force marched far and fights daily—they think us too weak to sally and will grow careless;

sentences.zh: 宜且勿出，示之以怯，鑿北城為突門二十餘道，俟其來至，列守未定，出其不意，直衝末柸帳，彼必震駭，不暇為計，破之必矣。

translations.literal: for now do not go out but show fear; cut more than twenty sally ports in the north wall, and when they come and their ranks are not yet set, strike Mozhe’s tent by surprise—they will be shaken and unable to respond, and he will surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: stay inside and seem afraid; cut twenty sally ports in the north wall; when they arrive unsettled, burst on Mozhe’s tent—they will panic and break.

sentences.zh: 末柸敗，則其餘不攻而潰矣。」

translations.literal: If Mozhe falls, the rest will collapse without a fight."
translations.idiomatic: If Mozhe falls, the rest will flee without fighting."

sentences.zh: 勒從之，密為突門。

translations.literal: Le agreed and secretly made the sally ports.
translations.idiomatic: Le agreed and secretly cut the sally ports.

sentences.zh: 既而疾陸眷攻北城，勒登城望之，見其將士或釋仗而寢，乃命孔萇督銳卒自突門出擊之，城上鼓以助其勢。

translations.literal: Soon Jilu attacked the north wall; Le mounted the wall and saw some soldiers lay down their arms and sleep; he ordered Kong Chang to lead crack troops out the sally ports while drums on the wall aided them.
translations.idiomatic: Jilu attacked the north wall. Le saw men sleeping on their arms and ordered Kong Chang’s elite out the sally ports with drums on the wall.

sentences.zh: 萇攻末柸逐之，入其壘門，為勒眾所獲，疾陸眷等軍皆退走。

translations.literal: Chang drove Mozhe into his camp gate and was seized by Le’s men; Jilu and the rest all retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Chang drove Mozhe to his gate where Le’s men seized him; Jilu’s army fled.

sentences.zh: 萇乘勝追擊，枕屍三十餘里，獲鎧馬五千匹。

translations.literal: Chang pursued, corpses lay for more than thirty li, and five thousand suits of armor and horses were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Chang pursued for thirty li, leaving corpses and taking five thousand horses and suits of armor.

sentences.zh: 疾陸眷收其餘眾，還屯渚陽。

translations.literal: Jilu gathered the remainder and returned to camp at Zhuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jilu gathered his survivors and withdrew to Zhuyang.

sentences.zh: 勒質末柸，遣使求和於疾陸眷，疾陸眷許之。

translations.literal: Le held Mozhe hostage and sent envoys seeking peace with Jilu; Jilu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Le held Mozhe hostage and sued for peace; Jilu agreed.

sentences.zh: 文鴦諫曰：「今以末柸一人之故而縱垂亡之虜，得無為王彭祖所怨，招後患乎！」

translations.literal: Wen Yang remonstrated, saying, "Now for the sake of one man Mozhe you release a foe on the brink of ruin—will this not anger Wang Pengzu and invite later trouble?"
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yang protested: "For one man you spare a dying foe—will not Wang Pengzu resent this and bring future trouble?"

sentences.zh: 疾陸眷不從，復以鎧馬金銀賂勒，且以末柸三弟為質而請末柸。

translations.literal: Jilu would not listen but again bribed Le with armor, horses, gold, and silver, and offered Mozhe's three younger brothers as hostages while requesting Mozhe.
translations.idiomatic: Jilu refused but bribed Le again with armor, horses, gold, and silver, offering Mozhe's three younger brothers as hostages to ransom Mozhe.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆勸勒殺末柸，勒曰：「遼西鮮卑健國也，與我素無仇讎，為王浚所使耳。

translations.literal: The generals all urged Le to kill Mozhe; Le said, "Liaoxi Xianbei are a strong state and have never been my enemy—they were sent by Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged killing Mozhe. Le said, "The Liaoxi Xianbei are a strong people and no enemy of mine—Jun sent them.

sentences.zh: 今殺一人而結一國之怨，非計也。

translations.literal: Now to kill one man and incur a whole state's hatred is no plan.
translations.idiomatic: Killing one man to earn a nation's hatred is folly.

sentences.zh: 歸之，必深德我，不復為浚用矣。」

translations.literal: Return him and they will deeply owe us and no longer serve Jun."
translations.idiomatic: Return him and they will owe us and cease serving Jun."

sentences.zh: 乃厚以金帛報之，遣石虎與疾陸眷盟於渚陽，結為兄弟。

translations.literal: Thereupon he richly repaid them with gold and silks, sent Shi Hu to ally with Jilu at Zhuyang, and they became sworn brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He sent rich gifts, had Shi Hu swear brotherhood with Jilu at Zhuyang, and they became sworn brothers.

sentences.zh: 疾陸眷引歸，王昌等不能獨留，亦引兵還薊。

translations.literal: Jilu withdrew; Wang Chang and the others could not remain alone and also led their troops back to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Jilu withdrew; Wang Chang could not stay and marched back to Ji.

sentences.zh: 勒召末柸，與之燕飲，誓為父子，遣還遼西。

translations.literal: Le summoned Mozhe, feasted and drank with him, swore father-and-son bond, and sent him back to Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Le feasted Mozhe, swore father-and-son ties, and sent him home to Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 末柸在塗，日南向而拜者三。

translations.literal: Mozhe on the road bowed southward three times a day.
translations.idiomatic: On the road Mozhe bowed south three times each day.

sentences.zh: 由是段氏專心附勒，王浚之勢遂衰。

translations.literal: Thereby the Duan clan devoted themselves to Le, and Wang Jun's power daily waned.
translations.idiomatic: The Duan clan then attached themselves to Le, and Jun's power waned.

sentences.zh: 游綸、張豺請降於勒。

translations.literal: You Lun and Zhang Chai requested surrender to Le.
translations.idiomatic: You Lun and Zhang Chai surrendered to Le.

sentences.zh: 勒攻信都，殺冀州刺史王象。

translations.literal: Le attacked Xindu and killed Inspector of Ji Wang Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Le attacked Xindu and killed Ji Inspector Wang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 浚復以邵舉行冀州刺史，保信都。

translations.literal: Jun again made Shao Ju acting Inspector of Ji and held Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Jun made Shao Ju acting Inspector of Ji and held Xindu.

sentences.zh: 是歲大疫。

translations.literal: That year there was a great pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: That year a great plague struck.

sentences.zh: 王澄少與兄衍名冠海內。

translations.literal: Wang Cheng in youth with his elder brother Yan had a fame that topped the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Wang Cheng and his brother Yan were famed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 劉琨謂澄曰：「卿形雖散朗，而內實動俠，以此處世，難得其死。」

translations.literal: Liu Kun said to Cheng, "Your form seems open and bright, yet inwardly you are restless and chivalric—with this you face the world, it will be hard to die a natural death."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun told Cheng, "You look open and bright, but inwardly you are restless and rash—you will not die in your bed."

sentences.zh: 及在荊州，悅成都內史王機，謂為己亞，使之內綜心膂，外為爪牙。

translations.literal: When he was in Jing Province he delighted in the Interior Administrator of Chengdu Wang Ji, treating him as his second, making him coordinate heart and sinew within and be claws and teeth without.
translations.idiomatic: In Jing Province he favored Chengdu Administrator Wang Ji as his second, using him as his right hand within and his fist without.

sentences.zh: 澄屢為杜弢所敗，望實俱損，猶傲然自得，無憂懼之意，但與機日夜縱酒博弈，由是上下離心；

translations.literal: Cheng was repeatedly defeated by Du Tao; reputation and substance both suffered, yet he remained arrogant and self-satisfied without worry, only drinking and gambling with Ji day and night—thereby superiors and inferiors lost heart;
translations.idiomatic: Tao defeated Cheng again and again; his reputation collapsed, yet he stayed arrogant, drinking and gambling with Ji day and night until his men lost heart;

sentences.zh: 南平太守應詹屢諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Administrator of Nanping Ying Zhan remonstrated repeatedly; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Nanping Administrator Ying Zhan remonstrated repeatedly; Cheng ignored him.

sentences.zh: 澄自出軍擊杜弢，軍於作塘。

translations.literal: Cheng himself led an army against Du Tao and encamped at Zuotang.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng marched against Du Tao and camped at Zuotang.

sentences.zh: 故山簡參軍王沖擁眾迎應詹為刺史，詹以沖無賴，棄之，還南平，沖乃自稱刺史。

translations.literal: The former aide of Shan Jian Wang Chong gathered a host to welcome Ying Zhan as inspector; Zhan thought Chong a scoundrel, abandoned him, and returned to Nanping; Chong then styled himself inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Former aide Wang Chong raised troops for Ying Zhan as inspector. Zhan spurned Chong as a ruffian and returned to Nanping; Chong proclaimed himself inspector.

sentences.zh: 澄懼，使其將杜蕤守江陵，徙治孱陵，尋又奔沓中。

translations.literal: Cheng was afraid, sent his general Du Rui to hold Jiangling, moved his seat to Canling, and soon fled to Tazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng sent Du Rui to hold Jiangling, moved to Canling, then fled to Tazhong.

sentences.zh: 別駕郭舒諫曰：「使君臨州雖無異政，然一州人心所繫，今西收華容之兵，足以擒此小丑，奈何自棄，遽為奔亡乎！」

translations.literal: Aide Gu Shu remonstrated, "My lord, though you have no special misrule in the province, the hearts of a whole province hang on you; now by gathering Huarong's troops in the west you could seize this petty foe—why abandon yourself and rush to flight?"
translations.idiomatic: Aide Gu Shu said, "The province looks to you. With Huarong's troops you could crush this bandit—why flee?"

sentences.zh: 澄不從，欲將舒東下。

translations.literal: Cheng would not listen and wished to take Shu east.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng refused and tried to take Shu east with him.

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「舒為萬里紀綱，不能匡正，令使君奔亡，誠不忍渡江。」

translations.literal: Shu said, "Shu is the registrar for ten thousand li and cannot set things right, making my lord flee—I truly cannot bear to cross the river."
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, "As registrar for the whole region I cannot watch you flee—I will not cross the Yangzi."

sentences.zh: 乃留屯沌口。

translations.literal: He remained encamped at Dunkou.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed at Dunkou.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王睿聞之，召澄為軍諮祭酒，以軍諮祭酒周顗代之，澄乃赴召。

translations.literal: Prince Rui of Langye heard and summoned Cheng as Army Adviser Sacrificial Officer, replacing him with the same-rank Zhou Yi; Cheng then answered the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui of Langye summoned Cheng as army adviser and replaced him with Zhou Yi; Cheng obeyed.

sentences.zh: 顗始至州，建平流民傅密等叛迎杜弢，苾別將王真襲沔陽，顗狼狽失據。

translations.literal: When Yi first reached the province, Fuling refugees Fu Mi and others rebelled to welcome Du Tao; Tao's detached general Wang Zhen raided Mianyang, and Yi was thrown into disorder and lost his footing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had barely arrived when Fuling refugees welcomed Du Tao; Tao's general Wang Zhen seized Mianyang and Yi lost his footing.

sentences.zh: 征討都督王敦遣武昌太守陶侃、尋陽太守周訪、歷陽內史甘卓共擊苾，敦進屯豫章，為諸軍繼援。

translations.literal: Campaign Commander Wang Dun sent Administrators Tao Kan, Zhou Fang, and Gan Zhuo together against Tao; Dun advanced to Yuzhang as rear support for the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun sent Tao Kan, Zhou Fang, and Gan Zhuo against Tao and advanced to Yuzhang in support.

sentences.zh: 王澄過詣敦，自以名聲素出敦右，猶以舊意侮敦。

translations.literal: Wang Cheng visited Dun and, because his fame had always stood above Dun's, still treated Dun with old contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng visited Dun and, thinking his fame greater, treated Dun with old contempt.

sentences.zh: 敦怒，誣其與杜苾通信，遣壯士扼殺之。

translations.literal: Dun was angry, slandered him for communicating with Du Tao, and sent braves to strangle him.
translations.idiomatic: Dun accused him of colluding with Tao and had him strangled.

sentences.zh: 王機聞澄死，懼禍，以其父毅、兄矩皆嘗為廣州刺史，就敦求廣州，敦不許。

translations.literal: Wang Ji heard Cheng was dead, feared disaster, and because his father Yi and brother Ju had both been Inspectors of Guangzhou, asked Dun for Guangzhou; Dun refused.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, fearing punishment, asked Dun for Guangzhou because his father and brother had held that post; Dun refused.

sentences.zh: 會廣州將溫邵等叛刺史郭訥，迎機為刺史，機遂將奴客門生千餘人入廣州。

translations.literal: Just then Guangzhou generals Wen Shao and others rebelled against Inspector Guo Na and welcomed Ji as inspector; Ji led more than a thousand retainers and students into Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou generals rebelled against Guo Na and welcomed Ji, who entered with a thousand retainers.

sentences.zh: 訥遣兵拒之，將士皆機父兄時部曲，不戰迎降，訥乃避位，以州授之。

translations.literal: Na sent troops to resist; the soldiers were all old followers of Ji's father and brother and would not fight but welcomed him in surrender; Na yielded the province.
translations.idiomatic: Na's troops were Ji's family veterans and surrendered; Na yielded the province.

sentences.zh: 王如軍中饑乏，官軍討之，其黨多降；

translations.literal: Wang Ru's army lacked food; when government troops attacked, many of his party surrendered;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru's army starved; under government attack many surrendered;

sentences.zh: 如計窮，遂降於王敦。

translations.literal: Ru's plans exhausted and he surrendered to Wang Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Ru, at his wits' end, surrendered to Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 鎮東軍司顧榮、前太子洗馬衛玠皆卒。

translations.literal: Eastern Garrison Chief Clerk Gu Rong and former Heir Apparent Attendant Wei Jie both died.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong and Wei Jie both died.

sentences.zh: 玠，瓘之孫也，美風神，善清談；

translations.literal: Jie was the grandson of Wei Guan, handsome in bearing and skilled in pure talk;
translations.idiomatic: Jie, grandson of Wei Guan, was handsome and famed for pure talk;

sentences.zh: 常以為人有不及，可以情恕，非意相干，可以理遣，故終身不見喜慍之色。

translations.literal: he often thought that when others fell short one could forgive by feeling, and when harm was not intended one could dismiss by reason—therefore in life he never showed joy or anger.
translations.idiomatic: he forgave human failings by sympathy and unintended slights by reason, and never showed anger or joy.

sentences.zh: 江陽太守張啟，殺行益州刺史王異而代之。

translations.literal: Administrator of Jiangyang Zhang Qi killed acting Inspector of Yi Wang Yi and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyang Administrator Zhang Qi killed acting Yi Inspector Wang Yi and replaced him.

sentences.zh: 啟，翼之孫也，尋病卒。

translations.literal: Qi was the grandson of Zhang Yi and soon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, grandson of Zhang Yi, soon died.

sentences.zh: 三府文武共表涪陵太守向沈行西夷校尉，南保涪陵。

translations.literal: The civil and military officers of the three offices jointly memorialized Administrator of Fuling Xiang Shen as acting Western Yi Commandant, guarding Fuling in the south.
translations.idiomatic: The three offices memorialized Fuling Administrator Xiang Shen as acting Western Yi Commandant to hold Fuling.

sentences.zh: 南安赤亭羌姚弋仲東徙榆眉，戎、夏襁負隨之者數萬；

translations.literal: The Chiting Qiang of Nan'an Yao Yizhong moved east to Yumei; tens of thousands of Rong and Xia followed carrying infants on their backs;
translations.idiomatic: Nan'an Chiting Qiang leader Yao Yizhong moved east to Yumei with tens of thousands of Rong and Han followers;

sentences.zh: 自稱護羌校尉、雍州刺史、扶風公。

translations.literal: he styled himself Protector of the Qiang, Inspector of Yong, and Duke of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: he styled himself Protector of the Qiang, Inspector of Yong, and Duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 孝愍皇帝上建興元年（

translations.literal: Above the Filial and Lamenting Emperor, first year of Jianxing (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Min of Jin, the first year of Jianxing (

sentences.zh: 癸酉，公元三一三年）

translations.literal: Guiyou, corresponding to the year 313 CE)
translations.idiomatic: the year Guiyou, 313 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁丑朔，漢主聰宴群臣於光極殿，使懷帝著青衣行酒。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day Dingchou, the Han ruler Cong feasted his ministers in the Hall of Extreme Light and made the Filial and Commiserating Emperor wear green robes and serve wine.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the new moon of the first month, Emperor Cong feasted his ministers in the Hall of Extreme Light and made Emperor Huai serve wine in green robes.

sentences.zh: 庾鈱、王俊等不勝悲憤，因號哭；

translations.literal: Yu Yin, Wang Jun, and others could not bear grief and wailed aloud;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yin, Wang Jun, and others wept aloud in grief;

sentences.zh: 聰惡之。

translations.literal: Cong hated this.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was disgusted.

sentences.zh: 有告鈱等謀以平陽應劉琨者，二月，丁未，聰殺鈱、俊等故晉臣十餘人，懷帝亦遇害。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Yin and others planned to respond to Liu Kun from Pingyang; in the second month, on the day Dingwei, Cong killed Yin, Jun, and more than ten former Jin ministers; the Filial and Commiserating Emperor was also murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused them of plotting with Liu Kun. On Dingwei in the second month Cong executed Yin, Jun, and more than ten former Jin ministers; Emperor Huai was murdered too.

sentences.zh: 大赦，復以會稽劉夫人為貴人。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed, and the Lady of Kuaiji Liu was again made Noble Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Cong proclaimed amnesty and restored Lady Liu of Kuaiji as noble lady.

sentences.zh: 荀崧曰：懷帝天姿清劭，少著英猷，若遇承平，足為守文佳主。

translations.literal: Xun Song said: The Filial and Commiserating Emperor was clear and keen by nature and in youth showed heroic plans; had he met peaceful times he would fully have been a fine guardian-text ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Song wrote: Emperor Huai was keen and talented; in peaceful times he would have been a fine guardian emperor.

sentences.zh: 而繼惠帝擾亂之後，東海專政，故無幽、厲之釁而有流亡之禍矣！

translations.literal: Yet he followed after the disorders of Emperor Hui, with the Prince of Donghai monopolizing government—therefore he had not the faults of You and Li but suffered the calamity of exile!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he followed Emperor Hui's chaos under the Prince of Donghai's rule, and though without You and Li's vices suffered exile and death.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，漢太后張氏卒，謚曰光獻。

translations.literal: On the day Yihai the Han Empress Dowager Zhang died; her posthumous title was Guangxian.
translations.idiomatic: On Yihai Empress Dowager Zhang died, posthumous name Guangxian.

sentences.zh: 張後不勝哀，丁丑，亦卒，謚曰武孝。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang could not bear the grief; on Dingchou she too died; her posthumous title was Wuxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang died of grief on Dingchou, posthumous name Wuxiao.

sentences.zh: 己卯，漢定襄忠穆公王彰卒。

translations.literal: On Jimao the Han Duke of Dingxiang, Loyal and Solemn Wang Zhang died.
translations.idiomatic: On Jimao Duke Wang Zhang of Dingxiang died.

sentences.zh: 三月，漢主聰立貴嬪劉娥為皇后，為之起皇□儀殿。

translations.literal: In the third month the Han ruler Cong installed Guibin Liu E as empress and built the Hall of Imperial Rites for her.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Cong made Guibin Liu E empress and built the Hall of Imperial Rites for her.

sentences.zh: 廷殿陳元達切諫，以為：「天生民而樹之君，使司牧之，非以兆民之命，窮一人之欲也。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Chen Yuanda remonstrated sharply in court, saying, "Heaven bore the people and set up rulers to govern them—not to stake the lives of the myriad on one man's desires.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Chen Yuanda remonstrated: "Heaven made rulers to shepherd the people—not to exhaust the realm for one man's pleasure.

sentences.zh: 晉氏失德，大漢受之，蒼生引領，庶幾息肩。

translations.literal: The Jin house lost virtue and Great Han received the mandate; the living crane their necks, hoping to rest their shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: Jin lost the mandate and Han received it; the people hoped at last to rest.

sentences.zh: 是以光文皇帝身衣大布，居無重茵，后妃不衣錦綺，乘輿馬不食粟，愛民故也。

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Guangwen wore coarse cloth, his dwelling had no double mats, consorts wore no brocade, and imperial horses ate no grain—because he loved the people.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwen wore coarse cloth, used no double mats, forbade brocade to consorts, and fed his horses no grain—out of love for the people.

sentences.zh: 陛下踐阼以來，已作殿觀四十餘所，加之軍旅數興，餽運不息，饑饉、疾疫，死亡相繼，而益思營繕，豈為民父母之意乎！

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne you have built more than forty halls and pavilions; moreover armies rise repeatedly, transport never ceases, famine and pestilence follow one another in death—yet you think more of construction. Is this the mind of a father and mother to the people!
translations.idiomatic: Since you ascended you have built forty halls; armies march endlessly, famine and plague kill multitudes—yet you build more. Is this how parents treat their children?

sentences.zh: 今有晉遺類，西據關中，南擅江表；

translations.literal: Now Jin remnants hold Guanzhong in the west and dominate the Yangzi south;
translations.idiomatic: Jin remnants hold Guanzhong and dominate the south;

sentences.zh: 李雄奄有巴、蜀；

translations.literal: Li Xiong holds Ba and Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong holds Ba and Shu;

sentences.zh: 王浚、劉琨窺窬肘腋；

translations.literal: Wang Jun and Liu Kun peer at your elbows and armpits;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun and Liu Kun watch your flanks;

sentences.zh: 石勒、曹嶷貢稟漸疏。

translations.literal: Shi Le and Cao Ni grow slack in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le and Cao Ni grow slack in tribute.

sentences.zh: 陛下釋此不憂，乃更為中宮作殿，豈目前之所急乎！
