translations.literal: Your Majesty sets aside these worries and builds a palace for the inner court—is this the present urgency!
translations.idiomatic: You ignore these threats to build the empress a palace—is that urgent now?

sentences.zh: 昔太宗居治安之世，粟帛流衍，猶愛百金之費，息露台之役。

translations.literal: In the past Emperor Taizong in an age of peace, with grain and silk flowing, still cherished the cost of a hundred gold pieces and halted the Terrace work.
translations.idiomatic: Even Taizong in peace, with grain flowing, halted the Terrace and cherished every hundred in gold.

sentences.zh: 陛下承荒亂之餘，所有之地，不過太宗之二郡，戰守之備，非特匈奴、南越而已。

translations.literal: Your Majesty inherits after great disorder; the land you hold is not two commanderies of Taizong's, and your defenses face more than Xiongnu and Nanyue alone.
translations.idiomatic: You rule after chaos on less than two of Taizong's commanderies, facing foes worse than Xiongnu and Nanyue.

sentences.zh: 而宮室之侈乃至於此，臣所以不敢不冒死而言也。」

translations.literal: Yet palace extravagance reaches this—I dare not fail to risk death in speaking."
translations.idiomatic: Yet palace luxury reaches this—I must speak though it cost my life."

sentences.zh: 聰大怒曰：「朕為天子，營一殿，何問汝鼠子乎，乃敢妄言沮眾！

translations.literal: Cong raged and said, "I am Son of Heaven and build one hall—why do you ratlings ask! You dare speak to discourage the host!
translations.idiomatic: Cong raged: "I am emperor and build one hall—why do you rats interfere! You discourage the host!

sentences.zh: 不殺此鼠子，朕殿不成！」

translations.literal: If I do not kill this ratling my hall will not be built!"
translations.idiomatic: If I do not kill this rat my hall will never rise!"

sentences.zh: 命左右：「曳出斬之！

translations.literal: He ordered the attendants, "Drag him out and behead him!
translations.idiomatic: He ordered, "Drag him out and behead him!

sentences.zh: 並其妻子同梟首東市，使群鼠共穴！」

translations.literal: His wife and children too—expose their heads together at the eastern market and let the rats share one burrow!"
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children too—expose them at the eastern market and let the rats share one hole!"

sentences.zh: 時聰在逍遙園李中堂，元達先鎖腰而入，即以鎖鎖堂下樹，呼曰：「臣所言者，社稷之計，而陛下殺臣。

translations.literal: Just then Cong was in the Hall of Regret in the Li grove of the Free Roaming Garden; Yuanda entered first with a chain at his waist, then chained himself to a tree below the hall and cried, "What your servant speaks is for the altars of state, yet Your Majesty kills your servant.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was in the Hall of Regret. Yuanda entered chained, locked himself to a tree, and cried, "I speak for the state and you kill me.

sentences.zh: 朱雲有言：『臣得與龍逢、比干游，足矣！』」

translations.literal: Zhu Yun said, 'Your servant may roam with Long Feng and Bi Gan—that is enough!'"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yun said one may die like Long Feng and Bi Gan—that is enough!"

sentences.zh: 左右曳之不能動。

translations.literal: The attendants dragged but could not move him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants could not drag him loose."

sentences.zh: 大司徒任顗、光祿大夫朱紀、范隆、驃騎大將軍河間王易等叩頭出血曰：「元達為先帝所知，受命之初，即引置門下，盡忠竭慮，知無不言。

translations.literal: Grand Minister Ren Yi, Palace Counselors Zhu Ji, Fan Long, and General of Agile Cavalry Prince Yi of Hejian and others kowtowed until they bled, saying, "Yuanda was known to the late emperor and at the beginning of the mandate was placed at the gate, exhausting loyalty and counsel without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yi, Zhu Ji, Fan Long, Prince Yi, and others kowtowed bleeding: "Yuanda served the late emperor faithfully from the start.

sentences.zh: 臣等竊祿偷安，每見之未嘗不發愧。

translations.literal: We privately steal salary and ease; whenever we see him we cannot but feel shame.
translations.idiomatic: We steal salary in ease and are shamed whenever we see him.

sentences.zh: 今所言雖狂直，願陛下容之。

translations.literal: Though his words are wild and straight, we pray Your Majesty will tolerate them.
translations.idiomatic: His words are blunt, but spare him.

sentences.zh: 因諫諍而斬列卿，其如後世何！」

translations.literal: To execute ranked ministers for remonstrance—what will posterity say!"
translations.idiomatic: Execute ministers for remonstrance—what will posterity say!"

sentences.zh: 聰默然。

translations.literal: Cong was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Cong fell silent.

sentences.zh: 劉後聞之，密敕左右停刑，手疏上言：「今宮室已備，無煩更營，四海未壹，宜愛民力。

translations.literal: Empress Liu heard and secretly ordered the attendants to halt the execution; she wrote by hand, "Palaces are already sufficient—no need to build more; the realm is not united—spare the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu secretly halted the execution and wrote: "Palaces suffice; the realm is not united—spare the people.

sentences.zh: 廷尉之言，社稷之福也，陛下宜加封賞；

translations.literal: The Commandant of Justice's words are the fortune of the altars; Your Majesty should add reward;
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant speaks for the state—you should reward him;

sentences.zh: 而更誅之，四海謂陛下何如哉！

translations.literal: to kill him instead—what will the realm think of Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: to kill him—what will the realm think!

sentences.zh: 夫忠臣進諫者固不顧其身也，而人主拒諫者亦不顧其身也。

translations.literal: Loyal ministers who advance counsel indeed do not consider their persons, and rulers who reject counsel also do not consider their persons.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers risk themselves; rulers who reject counsel risk themselves.

sentences.zh: 陛下為妾營殿而殺諫臣，使忠良結舌者由妾，遠近怨怒者由妾，公私困弊者由妾，社稷阽危者由妾，天下之罪皆萃於妾，妾何以當之！

translations.literal: Your Majesty kills remonstrators to build a hall for your concubine—let loyal tongues be silenced because of me, let near and far hate because of me, let public and private suffer because of me, let the altars totter because of me—all guilt in the realm gathers on me; how can I bear it!
translations.idiomatic: You kill remonstrators for my palace—let the realm's guilt fall on me!

sentences.zh: 妾觀自古敗國喪家，未始不由婦人，心常疾之。

translations.literal: I observe that states lost and houses ruined have never not been through women; I always hated this in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: States fall through women—I have always hated that.

sentences.zh: 不意今日身自為之，使後世視妾由妾之視昔人也！

translations.literal: I did not expect today to do it myself, making posterity view me as I viewed those of old!
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect to become what I despised!

sentences.zh: 妾誠無面目復奉巾櫛，願賜死此堂，以塞陛下之過！」

translations.literal: I truly have no face to serve again with comb and towel—I beg death in this hall to stop Your Majesty's fault!"
translations.idiomatic: I cannot serve again—grant me death here to atone for your fault!"

sentences.zh: 聰覽之變色。

translations.literal: Cong read it and changed color.
translations.idiomatic: Cong read it and turned pale.

sentences.zh: 任顗等叩頭流涕不已。

translations.literal: Ren Yi and the others kowtowed and wept without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yi and the others wept and kowtowed without end.

sentences.zh: 聰徐曰：「朕比年已來，微得風疾，喜怒過差，不復自制。

translations.literal: Cong said slowly, "In recent years I have had slight wind ailment; joy and anger exceed measure and I cannot control myself.
translations.idiomatic: Cong said slowly, "Lately I have had fits; joy and anger escape me.

sentences.zh: 元達，忠臣也。

translations.literal: Yuanda is a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanda is loyal.

sentences.zh: 朕未之察。

translations.literal: I did not perceive it.
translations.idiomatic: I did not see it.

sentences.zh: 諸公乃能破首明之，誠得輔弼之義也。

translations.literal: You gentlemen could break your heads to make it clear—truly the duty of assistants.
translations.idiomatic: You broke your heads to show me—true assistants.

sentences.zh: 朕愧戢於心，何敢忘之！」

translations.literal: I am ashamed and wary in heart—how dare I forget!"
translations.idiomatic: I am ashamed—how could I forget!"

sentences.zh: 命顗等冠履就坐，引元達上，以劉氏表示之，曰：「外輔如公，內輔如后，朕復何憂！」

translations.literal: He ordered Yi and the others to don caps and shoes and sit, brought Yuanda up, showed him the Liu memorial, and said, "Outer support like you, inner like the empress—what have I to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: He seated them, brought Yuanda up, showed Liu's letter: "With you outside and her within, what fear have I!"

sentences.zh: 賜顗等穀帛各有差，更命逍遙園曰納賢園，李中堂曰愧賢堂。

translations.literal: He gave Yi and the others grain and silk in varying measure, and renamed the Free Roaming Garden the Garden for Receiving Worthies and the Hall of Regret the Hall for Shaming Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He gave rewards and renamed the garden Garden for Receiving Worthies and the hall Hall for Shaming Worthies.

sentences.zh: 聰謂元達曰：「卿當畏朕，而反使朕畏卿邪！」

translations.literal: Cong said to Yuanda, "You ought to fear me—yet you make me fear you!"
translations.idiomatic: Cong told Yuanda, "You should fear me—yet you make me fear you!"

sentences.zh: 西夷校尉向沈卒，眾推汶山太守蘭維為西夷校尉。

translations.literal: Acting Western Yi Commandant Xiang Shen died; the masses pushed Administrator of Wenshan Lan Wei as Western Yi Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Western Yi Commandant Xiang Shen died; the people made Wenshan Administrator Lan Wei commandant.

sentences.zh: 維帥吏民北出，欲向巴東。

translations.literal: Wei led officials and people northward, intending to go toward Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei led his officials and people north, heading for Badong.

sentences.zh: 成將李恭、費黑邀擊，獲之。

translations.literal: Cheng generals Li Gong and Fei He intercepted and attacked; they captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng generals Li Gong and Fei He ambushed him and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙午，懷帝凶問至長安，皇太子舉哀，因加元服。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day bingwu: news of Emperor Huai's death reached Chang'an; the crown prince mourned and thereupon received the capping ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on bingwu day, word of Emperor Huai's death reached Chang'an; the crown prince went into mourning and was capped as an adult.

sentences.zh: 壬申，即皇帝位，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: Day renshen: he ascended the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day he took the throne, declared a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 以衛將軍梁芬為司徒，雍州刺史麴允為尚書左僕射、錄尚書事，京兆太守索綝為尚書右僕射、領吏部、京兆尹。

translations.literal: He made Guard General Liang Fen Grand Minister over the Masses, Yong Province Inspector Qu Yun Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Affairs, and Jingzhao Administrator Suo Lin Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, head of the Ministry of Personnel, and Jingzhao Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Guard General Liang Fen Grand Minister over the Masses, Yongzhou Inspector Qu Yun as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing with charge of secretariat affairs, and Jingzhao Administrator Suo Lin as Right Vice Director, head of the Ministry of Personnel, and Jingzhao Intendant.

sentences.zh: 是時長安城中，戶不盈百，蒿棘成林；

translations.literal: At this time in Chang'an city, households did not reach a hundred; wormwood and thorns formed groves;
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an then held fewer than a hundred households; weeds and thorns grew like forests;

sentences.zh: 公私有車四乘，百官無章服、印綬，唯桑版署號而已。

translations.literal: public and private together had four carriages; the hundred officials had no ceremonial robes, seals, or cords—only mulberry-wood boards for posting titles.
translations.idiomatic: the court and private households together owned four carts; officials had no court dress, seals, or ribbons—only mulberry boards on which to write their titles.

sentences.zh: 尋以索綝為衛將軍、領太尉，軍國之事，悉以委之。

translations.literal: Soon after, Suo Lin was made Guard General and concurrent Grand Commandant; military and state affairs were wholly entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Suo Lin was made Guard General and Grand Commandant as well; all military and civil affairs were placed in his hands.

sentences.zh: 漢中山王曜、司隸校尉喬智明寇長安，平西將軍趙染帥眾赴之；

translations.literal: Han Prince of Zhongshan Yao and Director of the Masters of Writing Qiao Zhiming raided Chang'an; General Who Pacifies the West Zhao Ran led troops to relieve it;
translations.idiomatic: Han Prince of Zhongshan Liu Yao and Director of the Masters of Writing Qiao Zhiming attacked Chang'an; General Who Pacifies the West Zhao Ran marched to its aid;

sentences.zh: 詔麴允屯黃白城以拒之。

translations.literal: an edict ordered Qu Yun to encamp at Huangbai City to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor ordered Qu Yun to hold Huangbai City against them.

sentences.zh: 石勒使石虎攻鄴，鄴潰，劉演奔廩丘，三台流民皆降於勒。

translations.literal: Shi Le sent Shi Hu to attack Ye; Ye collapsed; Liu Yan fled to Linqiu; the displaced people of the Three Terraces all surrendered to Le.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent Shi Hu against Ye; the city fell; Liu Yan fled to Linqiu; refugees from the Three Terraces all submitted to Le.

sentences.zh: 勒以桃豹為魏郡太守以撫之；

translations.literal: Le made Tao Bao Administrator of Wei Commandery to pacify them;
translations.idiomatic: Le appointed Tao Bao Administrator of Wei Commandery to settle them;

sentences.zh: 久之，以石虎代豹鎮鄴。

translations.literal: after a long while, he had Shi Hu replace Bao and garrison Ye.
translations.idiomatic: later he replaced Bao with Shi Hu to hold Ye.

sentences.zh: 初，劉琨用陳留太守焦求為兗州刺史，荀籓又用李述為兗州刺史；

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Kun had used Chenliu Administrator Jiao Qiu as Yan Province Inspector, and Xun Fan had also used Li Shu as Yan Province Inspector;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Kun had appointed Chenliu Administrator Jiao Qiu Yanzhou inspector, while Xun Fan had also named Li Shu to the same post;

sentences.zh: 述欲攻求，琨召求還。

translations.literal: Shu wished to attack Qiu; Kun summoned Qiu back.
translations.idiomatic: Shu tried to attack Qiu; Kun recalled Qiu.

sentences.zh: 及鄴城失守，琨復以劉演為兗州刺史，鎮廩丘。

translations.literal: When Ye fell, Kun again made Liu Yan Yan Province Inspector, garrisoning Linqiu.
translations.idiomatic: After Ye was lost, Kun again made Liu Yan Yanzhou inspector, stationed at Linqiu.

sentences.zh: 前中書侍郎郗鑒，少以清節著名，帥高平千餘家避亂保嶧山，琅邪王睿就用鑒為兗州刺史，鎮鄒山。

translations.literal: Former Palace Attendant Xi Jian, famed from youth for pure conduct, led more than a thousand households of Gaoping in flight to hold Mount Yi; Prince of Langye Rui thereupon employed Jian as Yan Province Inspector, garrisoning Mount Zou.
translations.idiomatic: Former Palace Attendant Xi Jian, known from youth for integrity, led over a thousand Gaoping families to refuge on Mount Yi; Prince of Langye Sima Rui then made him Yanzhou inspector, based on Mount Zou.

sentences.zh: 三人各屯一郡，兗州吏民莫知所從。

translations.literal: The three men each held one commandery; the officials and people of Yan Province did not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the three held a separate commandery; Yanzhou's officials and people did not know whom to obey.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王睿以前廬江內史華譚為軍咨祭酒。

translations.literal: Prince of Langye Rui made former Lujiang Interior Minister Hua Tan Army Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Langye Sima Rui made former Lujiang interior minister Hua Tan his army adviser.

sentences.zh: 譚嘗在壽春依周馥。

translations.literal: Tan had once relied on Zhou Fu while at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Tan had once depended on Zhou Fu at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 睿謂譚曰：「周祖宣何故反？」

translations.literal: Rui said to Tan, "Why did Zuoxuan Zhou rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: Rui asked Tan, "Why did Zhou Zuoxuan rebel?"

sentences.zh: 譚曰：「周馥雖死，天下尚有直言之士。

translations.literal: Tan said, "Though Zhou Fu is dead, the realm still has men who speak plainly.
translations.idiomatic: Tan replied, "Though Zhou Fu is dead, the realm still has men who speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 馥見寇賊滋蔓，欲移都以紓國難，執政不悅，興兵討之，馥死未逾時而洛都淪沒。

translations.literal: Fu saw bandits spreading and wished to move the capital to ease the state's peril; the rulers were displeased and raised troops to punish him—Fu had not been dead a year when Luoyang fell.
translations.idiomatic: Fu saw invaders spreading and wanted to move the capital to ease the crisis; the court disapproved and marched against him—before a year had passed since his death, Luoyang was lost.

sentences.zh: 若謂之反，不亦誣乎！」

translations.literal: If that is called rebellion, is it not slander!"
translations.idiomatic: To call that rebellion—is it not slander!"

sentences.zh: 睿曰：「馥位為征鎮，握強兵，召之不入，危而不持，亦天下之罪人也。」

translations.literal: Rui said, "Fu's rank was expeditionary commander; he held strong troops; summoned, he would not enter; in peril he would not support—these too are crimes against the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Rui said, "Fu was a frontier commander with a strong army; when summoned he would not come; in peril he gave no support—he too was guilty before the realm."

sentences.zh: 譚曰：「然，危而不持，當與天下共受其責，非但馥也。」

translations.literal: Tan said, "So—in peril and giving no support, the realm should bear the blame together, not Fu alone."
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "True—in peril with no support, the blame belongs to all, not to Fu alone."

sentences.zh: 睿參佐多避事自逸，錄事參軍陳頵言於睿曰：「洛中承平之時，朝士以小心恭恪為凡俗，以偃蹇倨肆為優雅，流風相染，以至敗國。

translations.literal: Many of Rui's aides shirked duty for ease; Recording Secretary Chen Bin said to Rui, "In Luoyang's days of peace, courtiers took cautious reverence for vulgarity and arrogant insolence for elegance; the current infected one another until the state was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Rui's staff avoided duty; recording secretary Chen Bin told him, "In Luoyang's peaceful days, courtiers treated caution as vulgar and arrogance as refinement; the fashion spread until the state fell.

sentences.zh: 今僚屬皆承西台餘弊，養望自高，是前車已覆而後車又將尋之也。

translations.literal: Now the staff all inherit the Western Terrace's leftover abuses, nursing reputation and holding themselves high—it is the cart ahead overturned and the cart behind about to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Your staff now inherit the old capital's bad habits, cultivating reputation and pride—the front cart has overturned and the rear is about to follow.

sentences.zh: 請自今臨使稱疾者，皆免官。」

translations.literal: I ask that from now on all who on assignment claim illness be dismissed from office."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, dismiss any envoy who feigns illness."

sentences.zh: 睿不從。

translations.literal: Rui did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Rui refused.

sentences.zh: 三王之誅趙王倫也，制《己亥格》以賞功，自是循而用之。

translations.literal: When the Three Princes executed Prince of Zhao Lun, they made the "Jihai Register" to reward merit; from then on it was followed and used.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Princes killed Prince of Zhao Sima Lun, they drew up the Jihai Register to reward merit; thereafter it was applied routinely.

sentences.zh: 頵上言：「昔趙王篡逆，惠皇失位，三王起兵討之，故厚賞以懷向義之心。

translations.literal: Bin memorialized, "Formerly Prince of Zhao usurped and rebelled; Emperor Hui lost the throne; the Three Princes raised troops to punish him—hence generous rewards to win hearts inclined to righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Bin argued, "When Prince of Zhao usurped the throne and Emperor Hui was deposed, the Three Princes rose to punish him—hence lavish rewards to win loyal hearts.

sentences.zh: 今功無大小，皆以格斷，乃至金紫佩士卒之身，符策委僕隸之門，非所以重名器，正紀綱也，請一切停之！」

translations.literal: Now merit great and small is all cut off by the register, until gold seals and purple cords hang on common soldiers and tally-documents rest in servants' hands—this is not how to honor names and vessels or rectify discipline; I ask that it all be stopped!
translations.idiomatic: Now every deed, great or small, is fixed by that register—gold seals on privates, tallies in servants' hands—this does not honor rank or uphold law; abolish it all!

sentences.zh: 頵出於寒微，數為正論，府中多惡之，出頵為譙郡太守。

translations.literal: Bin came from humble origins and often spoke righteous words; many in the headquarters hated him; he was sent out as Administrator of Qiao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was of humble birth and often spoke plainly; many in headquarters disliked him and had him posted as Qiao commandery administrator.

sentences.zh: 吳興太守周玘，宗族強盛，琅邪王睿頗疑憚之。

translations.literal: Administrator of Wuxing Zhou Qi—his clan was powerful; Prince of Langye Rui was quite wary of him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxing administrator Zhou Qi came from a powerful clan; Prince of Langye Sima Rui was wary of him.

sentences.zh: 睿左右用事者，多中州亡官失守之士，駕御吳人，吳人頗怨。

translations.literal: Many of those around Rui who held power were Central Plains officials who had lost their posts and holds; they looked down on Wu men, and Wu men were quite resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Rui's favorites were displaced officials from the central plains who lorded it over the Wu men, who grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 玘自以失職，又為刁協所輕，恥恚愈甚，乃陰與其黨謀誅執政，以諸南士代之。

translations.literal: Qi himself felt he had lost his post and was also slighted by Diao Xie; shame and rage grew worse; he secretly plotted with his faction to kill the rulers and replace them with southern gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Qi felt demoted and was slighted by Diao Xie; humiliated, he secretly plotted with his followers to kill the northerners in power and put southerners in their place.

sentences.zh: 事洩，玘憂憤而卒；

translations.literal: The affair leaked; Qi, worried and enraged, died;
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered; Qi died of grief and anger;

sentences.zh: 將死，謂其子勰曰：「殺我者，諸傖子也；

translations.literal: on the verge of death he told his son Mi, "Those who kill me are the northern riffraff;
translations.idiomatic: dying, he told his son Mi, "My killers will be those northern upstarts;

sentences.zh: 能復之，乃吾子也。」

translations.literal: he who can avenge me is my son."
translations.idiomatic: only a son who avenges me is truly my son."

sentences.zh: 石勒攻李惲於上白，斬之。

translations.literal: Shi Le attacked Li Yun at Shangbai and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le attacked Li Yun at Shangbai and killed him.

sentences.zh: 王浚復以薄盛為青州刺史。

translations.literal: Wang Jun again made Bo Sheng Qing Province Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun again appointed Bo Sheng Qingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 王浚使棗嵩督諸軍屯易水，召段疾陸眷，欲與之共擊石勒。

translations.literal: Wang Jun sent Zao Song to command the armies encamped at Yishui and summoned Duan Jilujuan, wishing to join him in attacking Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun sent Zao Song to camp the armies at Yishui and summoned Duan Jilujuan to join him against Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 疾陸眷不至，浚怒，以重幣賂拓跋猗盧，並檄慕容廆等共討疾陸眷。

translations.literal: Jilujuan did not come; Jun was angry and bribed Tuoba Yilu heavily, also issuing orders to Murong Hui and others jointly to attack Jilujuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jilujuan did not come; Jun, furious, lavished gifts on Tuoba Yilu and called on Murong Hui and others to attack Jilujuan together.

sentences.zh: 猗盧遣右賢王六修將兵會之，為疾陸眷所敗。

translations.literal: Yilu sent Right Worthy King Liu Xiu with troops to join him; they were defeated by Jilujuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu sent Right Worthy King Liu Xiu to join the campaign; Jilujuan defeated them.

sentences.zh: 廆遣慕容翰攻段氏，取徒河、新城，至陽樂，聞六修敗而還，翰因留鎮徒河，壁青山。

translations.literal: Hui sent Murong Han to attack the Duan, taking Tuhe and Xincheng; reaching Yangyue, he heard Liu Xiu had been defeated and returned; Han thereupon remained to garrison Tuhe, fortifying Qingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent Murong Han against the Duan, taking Tuhe and Xincheng; at Yangyue he learned of Liu Xiu's defeat and turned back; Han stayed to hold Tuhe and walled Qingshan.

sentences.zh: 初，中國士民避亂者，多北依王浚，浚不能存撫，又政法不立，士民往往復去之。

translations.literal: Earlier, scholars and commoners of China fleeing turmoil mostly went north to rely on Wang Jun; Jun could not shelter and settle them, and his laws and government were not established; scholars and commoners often left him again.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chinese refugees had fled north to Wang Jun; he could neither protect nor govern them well, and many drifted away again.

sentences.zh: 段氏兄弟專尚武勇，不禮士大夫。

translations.literal: The Duan brothers valued martial valor alone and did not honor scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Duan brothers cared only for arms and slighted scholars.

sentences.zh: 唯慕容廆政事修明，愛重人物，故士民多歸之。

translations.literal: Only Murong Hui's government was well ordered and he cherished men of worth; therefore scholars and commoners mostly went to him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Murong Hui governed well and valued talent; so most refugees turned to him.

sentences.zh: 廆舉其英俊，隨才授任，以河東裴嶷、北平陽耽、廬江黃泓、代郡魯昌為謀主，廣平游邃、北海逄羨、北平西方虔、西河宋奭及封抽、裴開為股肱，平原宋該、安定皇甫岌、岌弟真、蘭陵繆愷、昌黎劉斌及封弈、封裕典機要。

translations.literal: Hui raised their outstanding men and assigned posts according to talent: Hedong Pei Ji, Beiping Yang Dan, Lujiang Huang Hong, and Dai Commandery Lu Chang as chief strategists; Guangping You Sui, Beihai Pang Xian, Beiping Xifang Qian, Xihe Song Shuang, and Feng Chou, Pei Kai as arms and legs; Pingyuan Song Gai, Anding Huangfu Ji, Ji's younger brother Zhen, Lanling Mou Kai, Changli Liu Bin, and Feng Yi, Feng Yu to manage vital affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hui recruited their best men to fit posts: Pei Ji of Hedong, Yang Dan of Beiping, Huang Hong of Lujiang, and Lu Chang of Dai as chief advisers; You Sui of Guangping, Pang Xian of Beihai, Xifang Qian of Beiping, Song Shuang of Xihe, and Feng Chou and Pei Kai as his right hand; Song Gai of Pingyuan, Huangfu Ji of Anding, Ji's brother Zhen, Mou Kai of Lanling, Liu Bin of Changli, and Feng Yi and Feng Yu for confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 裕，抽之子也。

translations.literal: Yu was Chou's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was Feng Chou's son.

sentences.zh: 裴嶷清方有干略，為昌黎太守，兄武為玄菟太守。

translations.literal: Pei Ji was pure in conduct and capable in planning; he was Administrator of Changli; his elder brother Wu was Administrator of Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji was upright and resourceful; he was Changli administrator; his brother Wu held Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 武卒，嶷與武子開以其喪歸，過廆，廆敬禮之，及去，厚加資送。

translations.literal: When Wu died, Ji and Wu's son Kai escorted the coffin home; passing Hui, Hui honored them with ceremony, and when they left he sent them off with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu died, Ji and Wu's son Kai bore the coffin home; passing Hui's seat, Hui received them with honor and sent them away with rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 行及遼西，道不通，嶷欲還就廆。

translations.literal: On the road in Liaoxi the way was blocked; Ji wished to return and join Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In Liaoxi the road was blocked; Ji wanted to turn back to Hui.

sentences.zh: 開曰：「鄉里在南，奈何北行！

translations.literal: Kai said, "Our homeland lies south—how can we go north!
translations.idiomatic: Kai said, "Our home is south—why go north!

sentences.zh: 且等為流寓，段氏強，慕容氏弱，何必去此而就彼也！」

translations.literal: Moreover we are alike exiles; the Duan are strong, the Murong weak—why leave this to go to that!
translations.idiomatic: We are both exiles; the Duan are strong, the Murong weak—why leave one master for another!

sentences.zh: 嶷曰：「中國喪亂，今往就之，是相帥而入虎口也。

translations.literal: Ji said, "China is in chaos; to go there now is to lead one another into the tiger's mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "China is in chaos; to go south now is to walk each other into the tiger's mouth.

sentences.zh: 且道遠，何由可達！

translations.literal: Moreover the road is far—how could we arrive!
translations.idiomatic: The road is long—how could we reach it!

sentences.zh: 若俟其清通，又非歲月可冀。

translations.literal: If we wait for clear passage, that too is not something months can promise.
translations.idiomatic: To wait until the way is safe may take more than months.

sentences.zh: 今欲求托足之地，豈可不慎擇其人。

translations.literal: Now to seek a place to set foot—how can we not carefully choose the man!
translations.idiomatic: When we seek a foothold, we must choose our patron with care.

sentences.zh: 汝觀諸段，豈有遠略，且能待國士乎！

translations.literal: Look at the various Duans—do they have far-reaching design, and can they treat men of the state as guests!
translations.idiomatic: Look at the Duans—have they long vision, or treat true gentlemen as guests!

sentences.zh: 慕容公修仁行義，有霸王之志，加以國豐民安，今往從之，高可以立功名，下可以庇宗族，汝何疑焉！」

translations.literal: Lord Murong cultivates benevolence and righteousness and has the ambition of a hegemon-king; moreover his state is rich and his people secure—if we go to him now, on high we may establish merit and name, below we may shelter our clans—what do you doubt!
translations.idiomatic: Lord Murong is humane and righteous, with the mind of a true king; his domain is rich and his people at peace—follow him and we may win glory above and shelter our kin below—what is there to doubt!

sentences.zh: 開乃從之。

translations.literal: Kai then followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Kai agreed and went with him.

sentences.zh: 既至，廆大喜。

translations.literal: When they arrived, Hui was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, Hui was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 陽耽清直沈敏，為遼西太守。

translations.literal: Yang Dan was pure, upright, deep, and keen; he was Administrator of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dan was upright, subtle, and sharp; he had been Liaoxi administrator.

sentences.zh: 慕容翰破段氏於陽樂，獲之，廆禮而用之。

translations.literal: Murong Han defeated the Duan at Yangyue and captured him; Hui honored him and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Han defeated the Duan at Yangyue and captured Dan; Hui honored him and took him into service.

sentences.zh: 游邃、逄羨、宋奭，皆嘗為昌黎太守，與黃泓俱避地於薊，後歸廆。

translations.literal: You Sui, Pang Xian, and Song Shuang had all been Administrators of Changli; with Huang Hong they took refuge in Ji; later they returned to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: You Sui, Pang Xian, and Song Shuang had all been Changli administrators; with Huang Hong they had fled to Ji and later joined Hui.

sentences.zh: 王浚屢以手書召邃兄暢，暢欲赴之，邃曰：「彭祖刑政不修，華、戎離叛。

translations.literal: Wang Jun repeatedly summoned by personal letter You Sui's elder brother Chang; Chang wished to go; Sui said, "Pengzu's punishments and government are not repaired; Chinese and barbarians alike desert him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun repeatedly summoned Sui's brother Chang by personal letter; Chang meant to go; Sui said, "Pengzu keeps no law; Chinese and barbarians alike abandon him.

sentences.zh: 以邃度之，必不能久，兄且盤桓以俟之。」

translations.literal: By my reckoning he cannot last long—brother, stay awhile and wait."
translations.idiomatic: He will not last—brother, wait a while."

sentences.zh: 暢曰：「彭祖忍而多疑，頃者流民北來，命所在追殺之。

translations.literal: Chang said, "Pengzu is cruel and suspicious; lately when refugees came north he ordered them pursued and killed wherever found.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Pengzu is cruel and suspicious; when refugees came north he ordered them hunted down.

sentences.zh: 今手書殷勤，我稽留不往，將累及卿。

translations.literal: Now his letter is earnest; if I linger and do not go, I will bring disaster on you.
translations.idiomatic: Now his letter is warm; if I delay, you will suffer too.

sentences.zh: 且亂世宗族宜分，以冀遺種。」

translations.literal: Moreover in chaotic times clans ought to divide, to hope for surviving seed."
translations.idiomatic: In chaos a clan should split its chances, to preserve some line."

sentences.zh: 遂從之，卒與浚俱沒。

translations.literal: He followed this and in the end perished with Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He went and in the end died with Jun.

sentences.zh: 宋該與平原杜群、劉翔先依王浚，又依段氏，皆以為不足托，帥諸流寓同歸於廆。

translations.literal: Song Gai, with Pingyuan's Du Qun and Liu Xiang, had first relied on Wang Jun, then on the Duan; both they judged unworthy of trust; they led the various exiles together to join Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Song Gai, Du Qun of Pingyuan, and Liu Xiang had served Wang Jun, then the Duan; finding neither trustworthy, they led their fellow exiles to Hui.

sentences.zh: 東夷校尉崔毖請皇甫岌為長史，卑辭說諭，終莫能致；

translations.literal: Eastern Yi Commandant Cui Bi asked Huangfu Ji to be Chief Clerk, speaking humbly to persuade him; in the end he could not be brought;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yi Commandant Cui Bi sought Huangfu Ji as chief clerk with humble pleas but could not win him;

sentences.zh: 廆招之，岌與弟真即時俱至。

translations.literal: Hui recruited him; Ji and his younger brother Zhen came at once together.
translations.idiomatic: Hui summoned him; Ji and his brother Zhen came at once.

sentences.zh: 遼東張統據樂浪、帶方二郡，與高句麗王乙弗利相攻，連年不解。

translations.literal: Liaodong's Zhang Tong held the two commanderies of Lelang and Daifang and fought the King of Goguryeo Upli for years without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tong of Liaodong held Lelang and Daifang and warred with Goguryeo's King Upli for years without end.

sentences.zh: 樂浪王遵說統帥其民千餘家歸廆，廆為之置樂浪郡，以統為太守，遵參軍事。

translations.literal: King Zun of Lelang persuaded Tong to lead his people, more than a thousand households, to join Hui; Hui set up Lelang Commandery for them, making Tong Administrator and Zun Army Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Lelang King Zun persuaded Tong to bring more than a thousand households to Hui; Hui established Lelang commandery, made Tong administrator, and Zun army adviser.

sentences.zh: 王如餘黨涪陵李運、巴西王建等自襄陽將三千餘家入漢中，梁州刺史張光遣參軍晉邈將兵拒之。

translations.literal: Wang Ru's remaining followers—Fuling's Li Yun and Brazil's Wang Jian and others—left Xiangyang with more than three thousand households and entered Hanzhong; Liang Province Inspector Zhang Guang sent Army Adviser Jin Miao with troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors of Wang Ru—Li Yun of Fuling and Wang Jian of Brazil among them—led three thousand-odd families from Xiangyang into Hanzhong; Liangzhou inspector Zhang Guang sent adviser Jin Miao to block them.

sentences.zh: 邈受運、建賂，勸光納其降，光從之，使居成固。

translations.literal: Miao accepted bribes from Yun and Jian and urged Guang to accept their surrender; Guang agreed and had them dwell at Chenggu.
translations.idiomatic: Miao took bribes from Yun and Jian and urged Guang to accept their surrender; Guang agreed and settled them at Chenggu.

sentences.zh: 既而邈見運、建及其徒多珍寶，欲盡取之，復說光曰：「運、建之徒，不修農事，專治器仗，其意難測，不如悉掩殺之。

translations.literal: Later Miao saw that Yun, Jian, and their followers had many precious things and wished to seize them all; he again said to Guang, "Yun, Jian, and their kind do not cultivate the fields but specialize in weapons—their intent is hard to fathom; better to seize and kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: Later Miao saw their wealth and wanted it all; he told Guang again, "Yun and Jian's people farm little and stock arms—their intent is unclear; kill them all.

sentences.zh: 不然，必為亂。」

translations.literal: Otherwise they will surely make trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise they will rebel."

sentences.zh: 光又從之。

translations.literal: Guang again agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Guang agreed again.

sentences.zh: 五月，邈將兵攻運、建，殺之。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Miao led troops to attack Yun and Jian and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Miao attacked Yun and Jian and killed them.

sentences.zh: 建婿楊虎收餘眾擊光，屯於厄水；

translations.literal: Jian's son-in-law Yang Hu gathered the remnant force and struck Guang, encamping at Eshui;
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son-in-law Yang Hu rallied the survivors and attacked Guang, encamping on the E River;

sentences.zh: 光遣其子孟萇討之，不克。

translations.literal: Guang sent his son Meng Chang to attack him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Guang sent his son Meng Chang against him but failed.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以琅邪王睿為左丞相、大都督，督陝東諸軍事；

translations.literal: Day renchen: Prince of Langye Rui was made Left Chancellor, Grand Commander, and Supervisor of Military Affairs east of the passes;
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day Prince of Langye Sima Rui was made Left Chancellor, Grand Commander, and supervisor of armies east of the passes;

sentences.zh: 南陽王保為右丞相、大都督，督陝西諸軍事。

translations.literal: Prince of Nanyang Bao was made Right Chancellor, Grand Commander, and Supervisor of Military Affairs west of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Nanyang Sima Bao was made Right Chancellor, Grand Commander, and supervisor of armies west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「今當掃除鯨鯢，奉迎梓宮。

translations.literal: The edict said, "Now we must sweep away the whale and minnow and welcome the imperial coffin.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "We must now destroy the enemy and bring home the late emperor's coffin.

sentences.zh: 令幽、并兩州勒卒三十萬直造平陽，右丞相宜帥秦、涼、梁、雍之師三十萬徑詣長安，左丞相帥所領精兵二十萬徑造洛陽，同赴大期，克成元勳。」

translations.literal: Order You and Bing provinces to muster three hundred thousand troops to march straight on Pingyang; the Right Chancellor should lead three hundred thousand from Qin, Liang, Liang, and Yong to go straight to Chang'an; the Left Chancellor should lead two hundred thousand picked troops of his command straight on Luoyang—all to keep the great appointment and accomplish the supreme merit."
translations.idiomatic: Muster three hundred thousand from You and Bing to strike Pingyang; the Right Chancellor shall lead three hundred thousand from Qin, Liang, Yong, and Liang straight to Chang'an; the Left Chancellor shall lead two hundred thousand elite troops on Luoyang—all to meet on the day appointed and win the supreme victory."

sentences.zh: 漢中山王曜屯蒲板。

translations.literal: Han Prince of Zhongshan Yao encamped at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Han Prince of Zhongshan Liu Yao held Puban.

sentences.zh: 石勒使孔萇擊定陵，殺田徽；

translations.literal: Shi Le sent Kong Chang to attack Dingling and kill Tian Hui;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent Kong Chang against Dingling and killed Tian Hui;

sentences.zh: 薄盛帥所部降勒，山東郡縣，相繼為勒所取。

translations.literal: Bo Sheng led his division in surrender to Le; commanderies and counties east of the mountains fell to Le one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Sheng surrendered with his troops; east of the mountains, counties submitted to Le in succession.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰以勒為侍中、征東大將軍。

translations.literal: Han ruler Cong made Le Palace Attendant and General Who Conquers the East.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Liu Cong made Le palace attendant and General Who Conquers the East.

sentences.zh: 烏桓亦叛王浚，潛附於勒。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan also rebelled against Wang Jun and secretly attached themselves to Le.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuhuan rebelled against Wang Jun and secretly joined Le.

sentences.zh: 六月，劉琨與代公猗盧會於陘北，謀擊漢。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Liu Kun and Duke of Dai Yilu met north of Xing and plotted to attack Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Liu Kun and Duke of Dai Tuoba Yilu met north of Xing to plan an attack on Han.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，琨進據藍谷，猗盧遣拓跋普根屯於北屈。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Kun advanced and held Langu; Yilu sent Tuoba Pugen to encamp at Beiqu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Kun advanced to Langu Valley; Yilu sent Tuoba Pugen to camp at Beiqu.

sentences.zh: 琨遣監軍韓據自西河而南，將攻西平。

translations.literal: Kun sent Supervising General Han Ju from Xihe southward to attack Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Kun sent Supervising General Han Ju south from Xihe to attack Xiping.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰遣大將軍粲等拒琨，驃騎將軍易等拒普根，蕩晉將軍蘭陽等助守西平。

translations.literal: Han ruler Cong sent Grand General Can and others to resist Kun; General of Agile Cavalry Yi and others to resist Pugen; General Who Sweeps Jin Yang and others to help hold Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Liu Cong sent Grand General Can and others against Kun; General of Agile Cavalry Yi against Pugen; General Who Sweeps Jin Yang and others to help defend Xiping.

sentences.zh: 琨等聞之，引兵還。

translations.literal: When Kun and the others heard this, they led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Kun withdrew.

sentences.zh: 聰使諸軍仍屯所在，為進取之計。

translations.literal: Cong ordered the armies still to encamp where they were, making plans for advance.
translations.idiomatic: Cong ordered his armies to hold their positions and prepare to advance.

sentences.zh: 帝遣殿中都尉劉蜀詔左丞相睿以時進軍，與乘輿會於中原。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Palace Interior Commandant Liu Shu to instruct Left Chancellor Rui to advance the army in season and meet the imperial carriage in the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Palace Interior Commandant Liu Shu to tell Left Chancellor Sima Rui to march north in due season and meet the imperial train in the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸亥，蜀至建康，睿辭以方平定江東，未暇北伐。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day guihai: Shu reached Jiankang; Rui declined on the grounds that he was still settling the lower Yangtze and had no leisure for a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guihai day, Shu reached Jiankang; Rui pleaded that he was still pacifying the lower Yangtze and could not march north.

sentences.zh: 以鎮東長史刁協為丞相左長史，從事中郎彭城劉隗為司直，邵陵內史廣陵戴邈為軍咨祭酒，參軍丹楊張闓為從事中郎，尚書郎穎川鐘雅為記室參軍，譙國桓宣為舍人，豫章熊運為主簿，會稽孔愉為手彖。

translations.literal: He made Eastern Garrison Chief Clerk Diao Xie Left Chief Clerk of the Chancellor, Attendant Gentleman Liu Wei of Pengcheng Director Upright, Interior Minister of Shaoling Dai Miao of Guangling Army Adviser, Dan'yang Zhang Kai Army Attendant, Masters of Writing Gentleman Zhong Ya of Yingchuan Recorder, Qiao Commandery Huan Xuan Retainer, Kuaiji Xiong Yuan Chief Clerk, and Kuaiji Kong Yu Hand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Eastern Garrison chief clerk Diao Xie left chief clerk of the chancellery, attendant gentleman Liu Wei of Pengcheng director upright, Shaoling interior minister Dai Miao of Guangling army adviser, Zhang Kai of Danyang attendant gentleman, Zhong Ya of Yingchuan recorder, Huan Xuan of Qiao retainer, Xiong Yuan of Kuaiji chief clerk, and Kong Yu of Kuaiji hand secretary.

sentences.zh: 劉隗雅習文史，善伺候睿意，故睿特親愛之。

translations.literal: Liu Wei was well versed in letters and history and skilled at reading Rui's intent; therefore Rui was especially fond of him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei knew letters and history and read Rui's mood well; Rui favored him accordingly.

sentences.zh: 熊遠上書，以為：「軍興以來，處事不用律令，競作新意，臨事立制，朝作夕改，至於主者不敢任法，每輒關諮，非為政之體也。

translations.literal: Xiong Yuan memorialized, holding that since military campaigns began, in handling affairs they did not use statutes and orders but competed in making new ideas, setting rules on the spot—made in the morning, changed by evening—until the responsible officials dared not bear the law and each time had to consult upstream; this is not the body of governing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Yuan wrote that since the wars began officials had ignored statute, inventing rules overnight and changing them by evening, until no one dared apply the law without approval—this was no way to govern.

sentences.zh: 愚謂凡為駁議者，皆當引律令、經傳，不得直以情言，無所依準，以虧舊典。

translations.literal: I humbly hold that all who make rebutting memorials should cite statutes and the classics; they must not speak from feeling alone with nothing to rely on, to impair the old canons.
translations.idiomatic: Every dissent, he urged, should cite law and canon, not bare opinion that erodes precedent.

sentences.zh: 若開塞隨宜，權道制物，此是人君之所得行，非臣子所宜專用也。」

translations.literal: If opening and closing follow convenience and expedient ways control things—that is what the ruler may do; it is not what ministers should monopolize."
translations.idiomatic: Flexible expedients belong to the throne, not to officials alone."

sentences.zh: 睿以時方多事，不能從。

translations.literal: Rui, because the time had many affairs, could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, busy with crises, would not agree.

sentences.zh: 初，范陽祖逖，少有大志，與劉琨俱為司州主簿。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zu Ti of Fanyang had great ambition from youth; he and Liu Kun were together Chief Clerks of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zu Ti of Fanyang had been ambitious from youth; he and Liu Kun had served together as chief clerks of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 同寢，中夜聞雞鳴，蹴琨覺曰：「此非惡聲也！」

translations.literal: They shared a bed; at midnight they heard the cock crow, kicked Kun awake and said, "This is not an ill sound!"
translations.idiomatic: They shared a bed; at midnight a cock crowed; Zu Ti kicked Kun awake and said, "That is no ill omen!"

sentences.zh: 因起舞。

translations.literal: and thereupon rose to dance.
translations.idiomatic: and they rose to practice sword-dance.

sentences.zh: 及渡江，左丞相睿以為軍咨祭酒。

translations.literal: When they crossed the river, Left Chancellor Rui made him Army Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yangtze, Left Chancellor Sima Rui made him army adviser.

sentences.zh: 逖居京口，糾合驍健，言於睿曰：「晉室之亂，非上無道而下怨叛也，由宗室爭權，自相魚肉，遂使戎狄乘隙，毒流中土。

translations.literal: Ti dwelt at Jingkou, gathered fierce fighters, and said to Rui, "The Jin house's disorder was not that above was without the Way and below resented and rebelled; it was because the imperial clan fought for power and devoured one another, until the barbarians seized the gap and poison flowed through the central land.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingkou Zu Ti gathered bold men and told Rui, "The Jin fell not because the throne was wicked and the people rebelled, but because the imperial clan tore itself apart until barbarians poured through the heartland.

sentences.zh: 今遺民既遭殘賊，人思自奮，大王誠能命將出師，使如逖者統之以復中原，郡國豪傑，必有望風響應者矣！」

translations.literal: Now the survivors have suffered ravage and the people wish to exert themselves; if Your Highness can command generals to go forth and let men like Ti lead them to recover the Central Plains, the commanderies' bold men will surely turn their wind to answer!
translations.idiomatic: The survivors hunger to fight back; if you send generals north under men like me, the gentry of every commandery will rally to you!

sentences.zh: 睿素無北伐之志，以逖為奮威將軍、豫州刺史，給千人廩，布三千匹，不給鎧仗，使自召募。

translations.literal: Rui had never had the will to campaign north; he made Ti General Who Displays Might and Yan Province Inspector, gave a ration for a thousand men, three thousand bolts of cloth, and no armor or weapons—let him recruit himself.
translations.idiomatic: Rui had no mind for the north; he made Zu Ti General Who Displays Might and Yanzhou inspector, gave rations for a thousand men and three thousand bolts of cloth, but no arms—Zu Ti must raise his own troops.

sentences.zh: 逖將其部曲百餘家渡江，中流，擊楫而誓曰：「祖逖不能清中原而復濟者，有如大江！」

translations.literal: Ti led his personal following, more than a hundred households, across the river; midstream he struck the oar and swore, "If Zu Ti cannot clear the Central Plains and cross again, may the Great River be my witness!"
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti led his household guard—barely a hundred families—across the river; midstream he struck the oar and swore, "If I do not recover the north, may this river drown me!"

sentences.zh: 遂屯淮陰，起冶鑄兵，募得二千餘人而後進。

translations.literal: He thereupon encamped at Huaiyin, set up smelting and cast weapons, and recruited more than two thousand men before advancing.
translations.idiomatic: He camped at Huaiyin, forged arms, and mustered two thousand men before marching on.

sentences.zh: 胡亢性猜忌，殺其驍將數人。

translations.literal: Hu Kang was by nature suspicious and killed several of his fierce generals.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Kang was suspicious and killed several of his best generals.

sentences.zh: 杜曾懼，潛引王沖之兵使攻亢。

translations.literal: Du Zeng was afraid and secretly led Wang Chong's troops to make them attack Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng, afraid, secretly brought Wang Chong's troops against Kang.

sentences.zh: 亢悉精兵出拒之，城中空虛，曾因殺亢而並其眾。

translations.literal: Kang led out all picked troops to resist; the city was empty; Zeng thereupon killed Kang and absorbed his host.
translations.idiomatic: Kang marched out with every picked man; the city was empty; Zeng killed him and took his army.

sentences.zh: 周顗屯潯水城，為杜苾所困；

translations.literal: Zhou Yi encamped at Xunshui City and was beset by Du Bi;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi held Xunshui city and was trapped by Du Bi;

sentences.zh: 陶侃使明威將軍朱伺救之，苾退保泠口。

translations.literal: Tao Kan sent General Who Displays Brightness Zhu Si to rescue him; Bi withdrew to hold Lengkou.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan sent General Who Displays Brightness Zhu Si to relieve him; Bi fell back to Lengkou.

sentences.zh: 侃曰：「苾必步向武昌。」

translations.literal: Kan said, "Bi is sure to march on Wuchang."
translations.idiomatic: Kan said, "Bi will surely strike Wuchang."

sentences.zh: 乃自徑道還郡以待之，苾果來攻。

translations.literal: He himself took the direct road back to his commandery to wait; Bi indeed came to attack.
translations.idiomatic: He took the short road home to wait; Bi came as he had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 侃使朱伺逆擊，大破之，苾遁歸長沙。

translations.literal: Kan sent Zhu Si to meet and strike; he routed Bi greatly; Bi fled back to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Kan sent Zhu Si to intercept and routed him; Bi fled to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 周顗出潯水投王敦於豫章，敦留之。

translations.literal: Zhou Yi left Xunshui and went to Wang Dun at Yuzhang; Dun kept him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi left Xunshui and joined Wang Dun at Yuzhang; Dun detained him.

sentences.zh: 陶侃使參軍王貢告捷於敦，敦曰：「若無陶侯，便失荊州矣！」

translations.literal: Tao Kan sent Army Adviser Wang Gong to report victory to Dun; Dun said, "Without Lord Tao, Jing Province would have been lost!"
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan sent adviser Wang Gong to report victory to Dun; Dun said, "Without Lord Tao, Jingzhou would be lost!"

sentences.zh: 乃表侃為荊州刺史，屯沔江。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized Kan as Jing Province Inspector, encamped on the Mian River.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized Kan as Jingzhou inspector, stationed on the Mian.

sentences.zh: 左丞相睿召周顗，復以為軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Rui summoned Zhou Yi and again made him Army Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Sima Rui recalled Zhou Yi and again made him army adviser.

sentences.zh: 初，氐王楊茂搜之子難敵，遣養子販易於梁州，私賣良人子一人，張光鞭殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Di king Yang Maosou's son Nandi sent an adopted son to trade in Liang Province and privately sold one good man's son; Zhang Guang flogged him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Di king Yang Maosou's son Nandi had sent a foster son to trade in Liangzhou and secretly sold a free man's child; Zhang Guang had him flogged to death.

sentences.zh: 難敵怨曰：「使君初來，大荒之後，兵民之命仰我氐活，氐有小罪，不能貰也？」

translations.literal: Nandi resented, saying, "When the lord first came, after great famine, the lives of soldiers and people depended on us Di to live; the Di have small faults—can they not be pardoned?
translations.idiomatic: Nandi protested, "When you first came, after the great famine, our Di kept your soldiers and people alive; a small Di offense cannot be forgiven?

sentences.zh: 及光與楊虎相攻，各求救於茂搜，茂搜遣難敵救光。

translations.literal: When Guang and Yang Hu fought each other, each asked Maosou for rescue; Maosou sent Nandi to save Guang.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang fought Yang Hu, each begged Maosou for aid; Maosou sent Nandi to help Guang.

sentences.zh: 難敵求貨於光，光不與。

translations.literal: Nandi asked goods from Guang; Guang did not give them.
translations.idiomatic: Nandi demanded payment from Guang; Guang refused.

sentences.zh: 楊虎厚賂難敵，且曰：「流民珍貨，悉在光所，今伐我，不如伐光。」

translations.literal: Yang Hu richly bribed Nandi and moreover said, "The refugees' precious goods are all with Guang; now if you attack me, better attack Guang."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu bribed Nandi heavily and said, "The refugees' treasure is all in Guang's hands; attack him, not me."

sentences.zh: 難敵大喜。

translations.literal: Nandi was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Nandi was delighted.

sentences.zh: 光與虎戰，使張孟萇居前，難敵繼後。

translations.literal: Guang fought Hu; he sent Zhang Meng Chang in the van and Nandi followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: Guang fought Hu with Zhang Mengchang in front and Nandi behind.

sentences.zh: 難敵與虎夾擊孟萇，大破之，孟萇及其弟援皆死。

translations.literal: Nandi and Hu attacked Meng Chang from both sides and routed him greatly; Meng Chang and his younger brother Yuan both died.
translations.idiomatic: Nandi and Hu caught Mengchang in a pincer and destroyed him; Mengchang and his brother Yuan both died.

sentences.zh: 光嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Guang held the city and defended himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guang shut himself in the city.

sentences.zh: 九月，光憤激成疾，僚屬勸光退據魏興。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Guang, in furious agitation, fell ill; his staff urged Guang to withdraw and hold Weixing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Guang fell ill with rage; his staff urged him to fall back on Weixing.

sentences.zh: 光按劍曰：「吾受國重任，不能討賊，今得死如登仙，何謂退也！」

translations.literal: Guang laid hand on his sword and said, "I received the state's heavy charge and could not punish the bandit; to die now is like ascending to immortals—what is withdrawal!
translations.idiomatic: Guang gripped his sword and said, "The state entrusted me with a great charge; I could not defeat the rebels; to die now is heaven—what talk of retreat!

sentences.zh: 聲絕而卒。

translations.literal: His voice ceased and he died.
translations.idiomatic: His voice broke and he died.

sentences.zh: 州人推其少子邁領州事，又與氐戰沒，眾推始平太守鬍子序領梁州。

translations.literal: The province's people pushed his youngest son Mai to lead provincial affairs; he again fought the Di and perished; the masses pushed Shiping Administrator Hu Zixu to lead Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: The province made his youngest son Mai governor; he fought the Di and died; they then made Shiping administrator Hu Zixu Liangzhou leader.

sentences.zh: 荀籓薨於開封。

translations.literal: Xun Fan died at Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Fan died at Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 漢中山王曜、趙染攻麴允於黃白城，允累戰皆敗，詔以索綝為征東大將軍，將兵助允。

translations.literal: Han Prince of Zhongshan Yao and Zhao Ran attacked Qu Yun at Huangbai City; Yun was defeated in repeated battles; an edict made Suo Lin General Who Conquers the East and sent troops to help Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Han Prince of Zhongshan Liu Yao and Zhao Ran attacked Qu Yun at Huangbai City; Yun lost battle after battle; the court made Suo Lin General Who Conquers the East and sent him to aid Yun.

sentences.zh: 王貢自王敦所還，至竟陵，矯陶侃之命，以杜曾為前鋒大都督，擊王沖，斬之，悉降其眾。

translations.literal: Wang Gong returned from Wang Dun's seat to Jingling and forged Tao Kan's order, making Du Zeng Grand Commander in the Van to attack Wang Chong, beheaded him, and all his host surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong, returning from Dun's camp to Jingling, forged Tao Kan's order, made Du Zeng vanguard commander, attacked Wang Chong, killed him, and absorbed his army.

sentences.zh: 侃召曾，曾不至。

translations.literal: Kan summoned Zeng; Zeng did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Kan summoned Zeng; he would not come.

sentences.zh: 貢恐以矯命獲罪，遂與曾反擊侃。

translations.literal: Gong feared being punished for the forged order and thereupon joined Zeng in turning to attack Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Gong, fearing punishment for the forgery, joined Zeng in attacking Kan.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，侃兵大敗，僅以身免。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Kan's army was greatly defeated; he barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Kan's army was shattered; he barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 敦表侃以白衣領職。

translations.literal: Dun memorialized Kan to hold office in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Dun reported Kan as serving in undress.

sentences.zh: 侃復帥周訪等進攻杜苾，大破之，敦乃奏復侃官。

translations.literal: Kan again led Zhou Fang and others in advance against Du Bi and routed him greatly; Dun then memorialized to restore Kan's office.
translations.idiomatic: Kan rallied Zhou Fang and others, crushed Du Bi, and Dun restored his rank.

sentences.zh: 漢趙染謂中山王曜曰：「麴允帥大眾在外，長安空虛，可襲也。」

translations.literal: Han Zhao Ran said to Prince of Zhongshan Yao, "Qu Yun leads a great host outside; Chang'an is empty and can be raided.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhao Ran told Prince of Zhongshan Liu Yao, "Qu Yun's main force is abroad; Chang'an is empty—strike it.

sentences.zh: 曜使染帥精騎五千襲長安，庚寅夜，入外城。

translations.literal: Yao sent Ran to lead five thousand picked cavalry to raid Chang'an; on the night of day gengyin they entered the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: Yao sent Ran with five thousand picked horsemen against Chang'an; on gengyin night they broke into the outer city.

sentences.zh: 帝奔射雁樓。

translations.literal: The emperor fled to the Shooting-Geese Tower.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fled to the Shooting-Geese Tower.

sentences.zh: 染焚龍尾及諸營，殺掠千餘人；

translations.literal: Ran burned the Dragon Tail and the various camps and killed and plundered more than a thousand people;
translations.idiomatic: Ran burned the Dragon Tail palace and the camps, killing and looting more than a thousand;

sentences.zh: 辛卯旦，退屯逍遙園。

translations.literal: at dawn on xinmao he withdrew to encamp at the Free Roaming Garden.
translations.idiomatic: at dawn on xinmao day he withdrew to the Free Roaming Garden.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，將軍麴鑒自阿城帥眾五千救長安。

translations.literal: Day renchen: General Qu Jian from A City led five thousand men to rescue Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day General Qu Jian marched five thousand men from A City to relieve Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，染引還，鑒追之，與曜遇於零武，鑒兵大敗。

translations.literal: Day guisi: Ran led the army back; Jian pursued and met Yao at Lingwu; Jian's army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day Ran withdrew; Jian pursued and met Yao at Lingwu; Jian's force was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 楊虎、楊難敵急攻梁州，鬍子序棄城走，難敵自稱刺史。

translations.literal: Yang Hu and Yang Nandi pressed the attack on Liang Province; Hu Zixu abandoned the city and fled; Nandi styled himself Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hu and Yang Nandi pressed Liangzhou; Hu Zixu fled the city; Nandi proclaimed himself inspector.

sentences.zh: 漢中山王曜恃勝而不設備。

translations.literal: Han Prince of Zhongshan Yao relied on victory and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Han Prince of Zhongshan Liu Yao, overconfident, kept no guard.

sentences.zh: 十一月，麴允引兵襲之，漢兵大敗，殺其冠軍將軍喬智明；

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Qu Yun led troops in a surprise attack; Han troops were greatly defeated and General Who Conquers the Champion Qiao Zhiming was killed;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Qu Yun surprised him; the Han army was routed and General Who Conquers the Champion Qiao Zhiming was killed;

sentences.zh: 曜引歸平陽。

translations.literal: Yao led the return to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao retreated to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 王浚以其父字處道，自謂應「當塗高」之讖，謀稱尊號。

translations.literal: Wang Jun, because his father's style was Chudao, considered himself to fulfill the omen "when the road is coated" and plotted to take the honored title.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, whose father's courtesy name was Chudao, thought himself the man of the prophecy "when the road is coated" and plotted to declare himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 前勃海太守劉亮、北海太守王摶、司空手彖高柔切諫，浚皆殺之。

translations.literal: Former Administrator of Bohai Liu Liang, Administrator of Beihai Wang Tuan, and Hand Secretary to the Minister of Works Gao Rou remonstrated sharply; Jun killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Former Bohai administrator Liu Liang, Beihai administrator Wang Tuan, and Minister of Works hand secretary Gao Rou protested fiercely; Jun killed them all.

sentences.zh: 燕國霍原，志節清高，屢辭征辟。

translations.literal: Huoyuan of Yan State—will and integrity pure and lofty—repeatedly declined summons and appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Huoyuan of Yan State, pure in will and conduct, had repeatedly refused office.

sentences.zh: 浚以尊號事問之，原不答。

translations.literal: Jun asked him about taking the honored title; Yuan did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Jun asked his view of the imperial title; Yuan would not answer.

sentences.zh: 浚誣原與群盜通，殺而梟其首。

translations.literal: Jun falsely charged Yuan with communicating with bandits, killed him, and exposed his head.
translations.idiomatic: Jun accused Yuan of collusion with bandits, killed him, and displayed his head.

sentences.zh: 於是士民駭怨，而浚矜豪日甚，不親政事，所任皆苛刻小人，棗嵩、朱碩，貪橫尤甚。

translations.literal: Thereupon scholars and commoners were alarmed and resentful, while Jun's arrogance grew daily; he did not personally handle government; those he employed were all harsh petty men—Zao Song and Zhu Shuo were especially greedy and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people were terrified and angry; Jun grew more arrogant, neglected government, and trusted harsh petty men—Zao Song and Zhu Shuo worst of all.

sentences.zh: 北州謠曰：「府中赫赫，朱丘伯；

translations.literal: A northern province ballad said, "In the headquarters, blazing bright—Zhu the hill lord;
translations.idiomatic: A northern ballad ran, "In the headquarters, blazing bright—Lord Zhu of the hill;

sentences.zh: 十囊、五囊，入棗郎。」

translations.literal: ten sacks, five sacks, enter the Zao lord."
translations.idiomatic: ten sacks, five sacks—all for young master Zao."

sentences.zh: 調發殷煩，下不堪命，多叛入鮮卑。

translations.literal: Levies and requisitions were frequent and heavy; those below could not bear the orders; many rebelled and entered the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes crushed the people; many fled to the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 從事韓鹹監護柳城，盛稱慕容廆能接納士民，欲以諷浚。

translations.literal: Attendant Han Xian oversaw Liucheng and greatly praised Murong Hui's ability to receive scholars and commoners, wishing to admonish Jun by it.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Han Xian, overseeing Liucheng, praised Murong Hui's welcome to refugees, hoping to shame Jun.

sentences.zh: 浚怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Jun was angry and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun killed him in anger.

sentences.zh: 浚始者唯恃鮮卑、烏桓以為強，既而皆叛之。

translations.literal: At first Jun had relied only on the Xianbei and Wuhuan for strength; afterward they all rebelled against him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had relied on Xianbei and Wuhuan strength; now they all deserted him.

sentences.zh: 加以蝗旱連年，兵勢益弱。

translations.literal: Locusts and drought continued for years; military strength grew weaker still.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts and drought ran on for years; his armies weakened further.

sentences.zh: 石勒欲襲之，未知虛實，將遣使覘之，參佐請用羊祜、陸抗故事，致書於浚。

translations.literal: Shi Le wished to raid him but did not know the true situation; he was about to send someone to reconnoiter; aides asked to use the precedents of Yang Hu and Lu Kang and send a letter to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le meant to strike him but needed intelligence; his staff urged the Yang Hu–Lu Kang precedent—a letter to Jun.

sentences.zh: 勒以問張賓，賓曰：「浚名為晉臣，實欲廢晉自立，但患四海英雄莫之從耳；

translations.literal: Le asked Zhang Bin; Bin said, "Jun's name is Jin minister but in fact he wishes to abolish Jin and stand alone—only he fears that heroes throughout the realm will not follow;
translations.idiomatic: Le consulted Zhang Bin; Bin said, "Jun is a Jin minister in name only; he wants the throne but fears no hero will follow him;

sentences.zh: 其欲得將軍，猶項羽之欲得韓信也。

translations.literal: his wish to gain the General is like Xiang Yu's wish to gain Han Xin.
translations.idiomatic: he wants you as Xiang Yu wanted Han Xin.

sentences.zh: 將軍威振天下，今卑辭厚禮，折節事之，猶懼不言，況為羊、陸之亢敵乎！

translations.literal: The General's prestige shakes the realm; if now with humble words and heavy gifts you bend your person to serve him, you still fear he will not speak—how much less rival Yang and Lu as enemies!
translations.idiomatic: Your fame fills the realm; bow to him with gifts and he may still ignore you—how can you play Yang Hu or Lu Kang against him!

sentences.zh: 夫謀人而使人覺其情，難以得志矣。」

translations.literal: To plot against a man and let him perceive your feeling—hard to achieve your aim."
translations.idiomatic: Once he sees your design, you will not succeed."

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「善！」

translations.literal: Le said, "Good!
translations.idiomatic: Le said, "Well said!

sentences.zh: 十二月，勒遣舍人王子春、董肇多繼珍寶，奉表於浚曰：「勒本小胡，遭世饑亂，流離屯厄，竄命冀州，竊相保聚以救性命。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Le sent Retainer Wang Zichun and Dong Zhao with many follow-on treasures, presenting a memorial to Jun, saying, "Le was originally a petty Hu; encountering age of famine and chaos, drifting in hardship and distress, hiding life in Ji Province, stealing mutual protection to save life.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Le sent retainer Wang Zichun and Dong Zhao laden with gifts and a memorial to Jun: "I am a humble barbarian, starving in chaos, clinging to life in Ji Province by banding with others for survival.

sentences.zh: 今晉祚淪夷，中原無主；

translations.literal: Now Jin's mandate is overthrown; the Central Plains has no lord;
translations.idiomatic: Jin's mandate is fallen; the Central Plains has no lord;

sentences.zh: 殿下州鄉貴望，四海所宗，為帝王者，非公復誰！

translations.literal: Your Highness is noble hope of your province and township, honored by all within the seas—who but you to be emperor!
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness is the hope of your homeland and the honor of the realm—who but you should be emperor!

sentences.zh: 勒所以捐軀起兵，誅討暴亂者，正為殿下驅除爾。

translations.literal: Le's reason for casting aside body and raising troops to punish and attack violent disorder is precisely to drive them away for Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: I took up arms only to clear Your Highness's path.

sentences.zh: 伏願殿下應天順人，早登皇祚。

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Highness to accord with Heaven and the people and early ascend the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to heed Heaven and the people and take the throne soon.

sentences.zh: 勒奉戴殿下如天地父母，殿下察勒微心，亦當視之如子也。」

translations.literal: Le supports Your Highness like Heaven and Earth and father and mother; Your Highness discerning Le's slight heart should also regard him as a son."
translations.idiomatic: I will serve you as son to father; regard me likewise as a son."

sentences.zh: 又遺棗嵩書，厚賂之。

translations.literal: He also sent Zao Song a letter and richly bribed him.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Zao Song as well and bribed him heavily.

sentences.zh: 浚以段疾陸眷新叛，士民多棄己去，聞勒欲附之，甚喜，謂子春曰：「石公一時英傑，據有趙、魏，乃欲稱籓於孤，其可信乎？」

translations.literal: Jun, because Duan Jilujuan had newly rebelled and scholars and commoners mostly abandoned him, heard that Le wished to attach himself and was greatly pleased; he said to Zichun, "Lord Shi is a hero of the age, holding Zhao and Wei—yet he wishes to declare himself a vassal to me; can this be believed?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun, with Jilujuan newly in revolt and his people deserting, was delighted that Le would submit; he asked Zichun, "Shi Le is a hero of the age, holding Zhao and Wei—yet he would be my vassal; can I trust this?"

sentences.zh: 子春曰：「石將軍才力強盛，誠如聖旨。

translations.literal: Zichun said, "General Shi's talent and strength are strong—truly as the sage decree says.
translations.idiomatic: Zichun said, "General Shi is mighty—as you say.

sentences.zh: 但以殿下中州貴望，威行夷、夏，自古胡人為輔佐名臣則有矣，未有為帝王者也。

translations.literal: But because Your Highness is noble hope of the central provinces, your prestige extending to barbarian and Chinese—since antiquity there have been Hu men as famous assisting ministers, but none who became emperor.
translations.idiomatic: But Your Highness is the central plains' true lord, feared by Chinese and barbarian alike—barbarians have served as great ministers, never as emperors.

sentences.zh: 石將軍非惡帝王不為而讓於殿下，顧以帝王自有歷數，非智力之所取，雖強取之，必不為天人之所與故也。

translations.literal: General Shi does not hate being emperor and yield to Your Highness—only he considers that emperorship has its allotted turn, not something wit and force can seize; though taken by strength, Heaven and men will not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: General Shi does not scorn the throne but yields to you—he knows the mandate is not won by force alone; seize it by strength and Heaven will deny you.

sentences.zh: 項羽雖強，終為漢有。

translations.literal: Though Xiang Yu was strong, in the end Han possessed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu was strong, yet Han possessed the realm.

sentences.zh: 石將軍之比殿下，猶陰精之與太陽，是以遠鑒前事，歸身殿下，此乃石將軍之明識所以遠過於人也，殿下又何怪乎！」

translations.literal: General Shi compared with Your Highness is like yin essence to the sun—therefore, discerning past affairs from afar, he gives his person to Your Highness; this is General Shi's bright knowledge surpassing others by far—why should Your Highness wonder!"
translations.idiomatic: General Shi beside you is moon to sun—reading history, he bows to you; that is wisdom beyond others—why wonder!"

sentences.zh: 浚大悅，封子春、肇皆為列侯，遣使報聘，以厚幣酬之。

translations.literal: Jun was greatly pleased, enfeoffed Zichun and Zhao as ranked marquises, sent envoys in return visit, and repaid with heavy gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was overjoyed, enfeoffed Zichun and Zhao as marquises, sent envoys in return, and repaid with rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 游綸兄統，為浚司馬，鎮范陽，遣使私附於勒；

translations.literal: You Sui's elder brother Tong was Jun's Marshal, holding Fanyang; he sent an envoy privately to attach to Le;
translations.idiomatic: You Sui's brother Tong, Jun's marshal at Fanyang, secretly sent envoys to Le;

sentences.zh: 勒斬其使以送浚。

translations.literal: Le beheaded the envoy and sent him to Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Le killed the envoy and sent the head to Jun.

sentences.zh: 浚雖不罪統，益信勒為忠誠，無復疑矣。

translations.literal: Though Jun did not punish Tong, he trusted Le all the more as loyal and had no further doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Jun did not punish Tong but trusted Le completely and doubted no more.

sentences.zh: 是歲，左丞相睿遣世子紹鎮廣陵，以丞相手彖蔡謨為參軍。

translations.literal: This year Left Chancellor Rui sent the heir apparent Shao to garrison Guangling and made Chancellor's Hand Secretary Cai Mo Army Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: That year Left Chancellor Sima Rui sent heir apparent Shao to hold Guangling and made chancellor's hand secretary Cai Mo his adviser.

sentences.zh: 謨，克之子也。

translations.literal: Mo was Ke's son.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was the son of Cai Ke.

sentences.zh: 漢中山王曜圍河南尹魏浚於石樑，兗州刺史劉演、河內太守郭默遣兵救之，曜分兵逆戰於河北，敗之；

translations.literal: Han Prince of Zhongshan Yao besieged Henan Intendant Wei Jun at Shiliang; Yan Province Inspector Liu Yan and Henei Administrator Guo Mo sent troops to rescue him; Yao divided troops to meet and fight on the north of the river and defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: Han Prince of Zhongshan Liu Yao besieged Henan intendant Wei Jun at Shiliang; Yanzhou inspector Liu Yan and Henei administrator Guo Mo sent relief; Yao met them north of the river and defeated them;

sentences.zh: 浚夜走，獲而殺之。

translations.literal: Jun fled by night; they captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun fled by night; they caught and killed him.

sentences.zh: 代公猗盧城盛樂以為北都，治故平城為南都；

translations.literal: Duke of Dai Yilu walled Shengle as the Northern Capital and governed the old Pingcheng as the Southern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Dai Tuoba Yilu fortified Shengle as northern capital and kept old Pingcheng as southern capital;

sentences.zh: 又作新平城於灅水之陽，使右賢王六修鎮之，統領南部。

translations.literal: he also built New Pingcheng on the south bank of the Chishui and sent Right Worthy King Liu Xiu to garrison it, overseeing the southern region.
translations.idiomatic: he built New Pingcheng on the south bank of the Chishui and posted Right Worthy King Liu Xiu there to rule the south.
